item.title: OpenAI previews GPT-5.6 Sol, a next-generation model with enhanced coding, science, and cybersecurity capabilities and advanced safety features [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced GPT-5.6 Sol, a next-generation AI model that offers enhanced capabilities in coding, scientific research, and cybersecurity. This model also incorporates OpenAI's most advanced safety features to ensure responsible and secure use. GPT-5.6 Sol builds on previous versions by improving performance in specialized technical domains, aiming to support complex problem-solving and innovation. The integration of a robust safety stack reflects OpenAI's commitment to mitigating risks associated with powerful AI technologies. The release of GPT-5.6 Sol signals continued progress in AI development, with potential impacts across various industries that rely on advanced computational tools. OpenAI's focus on safety may influence future standards for AI deployment and governance.

item.title: OpenAI says US government will vet users of its GPT-5.6 AI model starting in 2026
item.description: OpenAI announced that starting in 2026, the U.S. government will vet users of its upcoming GPT-5.6 AI model. This new policy aims to regulate access to the advanced AI technology to address concerns about its potential misuse and ensure responsible deployment. The vetting process will involve government oversight to screen individuals and organizations seeking to use GPT-5.6, reflecting increased regulatory attention on powerful AI systems. OpenAI's decision highlights ongoing efforts to balance innovation with safety and ethical considerations in AI development.

item.title: US Commerce Department allows Anthropic to release Claude Mythos 5 AI model to over 100 trusted US companies and government agencies [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: The US Commerce Department has lifted its export controls on Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 AI model, permitting its release to over 100 trusted US companies and government agencies. This decision reverses a recent block imposed due to security concerns and marks a significant step in the US government's approach to regulating advanced AI technologies. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick cited substantial progress in discussions with Anthropic, noting the company's commitment to collaborate on protocols and standards for AI model releases. While the release of Mythos 5 is authorized, the status of the related Fable 5 model remains uncertain, with talks ongoing regarding its potential availability. This development reflects the US government's efforts to balance maintaining leadership in AI innovation with safeguarding national security. The new regulatory framework grants the government oversight of frontier AI models, affecting access for international partners and raising concerns among allies about dependency on US decisions.

item.title: Analysis shows the performance gap between open weights and closed source LLMs varies by benchmark, with coding benchmarks narrowing gap to 1-2 months by mid-2026 while others remain around 5 months [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: An analysis of the performance gap between open weights and closed source large language models (LLMs) reveals that this gap varies depending on the benchmark used. While coding benchmarks show a significant narrowing of the gap, reducing it to about one to two months by mid-2026, other benchmarks indicate the gap remains around five months. This suggests that open source models are catching up to closed source models at different rates across various tasks. The study examined 18 different benchmarks from the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, finding that improvements in coding capabilities have driven much of the progress in open source LLMs. However, the average gap across all benchmarks has remained relatively stable over time. This highlights the complexity of measuring LLM quality and suggests that predictions about open source models matching closed source ones depend heavily on the chosen evaluation metrics.

item.title: Researchers debate AI's impact on mathematics, exploring how AI-assisted problem solving may reshape the role and purpose of mathematicians [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers are examining how artificial intelligence is transforming mathematics, particularly through AI-assisted problem solving that could change the traditional role and purpose of mathematicians. Prominent figures like Terence Tao envision a future where humans and AI collaborate on complex mathematical challenges, potentially ushering in an era of "Big Mathematics." This shift raises questions about the nature of mathematical discovery and the value of human intuition and creativity in the field. Historically, mathematicians have relied on deep contemplation and creative reasoning to formulate and prove conjectures, a process that AI is beginning to accelerate and, in some cases, automate. Recent advances in AI, including systems that perform at the level of top high school mathematicians, demonstrate the technology's growing capability to tackle difficult problems. This evolution prompts ongoing debate about how AI will reshape mathematical research, the experience of mathematicians, and the future of the discipline itself.

item.title: Weave launches a smart model routing proxy for Claude, Codex, and Cursor that selects the best AI model per request with local key encryption and observability [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Weave has launched a smart model routing proxy that selects the best AI model for each request, supporting Claude, Codex, Cursor, and other platforms. This proxy uses a local embedder to route requests efficiently across multiple providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini, while keeping API keys encrypted on the user's device. It also offers observability features with built-in tracing and dashboard integration. The router supports various AI models and APIs, including open-source options via OpenRouter, and can be easily integrated with existing tools through simple commands or self-hosted setups. It provides flexibility with per-request routing decisions, streaming support, and compatibility with multiple AI service APIs, making it a versatile solution for managing AI model usage. By enabling local key encryption and detailed observability, Weave's router enhances security and transparency for users managing multiple AI models. Its design aims to optimize model selection dynamically, potentially improving performance and cost-efficiency for developers and organizations using diverse AI services.

item.title: Reports show students in East Asia using AI-powered smart glasses to cheat in exams, prompting education authorities to consider stricter screening and new anti-cheating measures [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Students in East Asia have been reported using AI-powered smart glasses to cheat during exams, raising concerns about academic integrity in the region's highly competitive educational environment. Incidents in South Korea and Taiwan have prompted education authorities to consider stricter screening measures and update anti-cheating protocols to address this emerging challenge. These smart glasses can discreetly display information and interact with AI models, making traditional exam monitoring more difficult. In response, countries like China and the UK have increased inspections and warnings about the potential for AI-enabled devices to facilitate cheating. Experts warn that as these technologies become more advanced and widespread, education systems will need to adapt their assessment methods to maintain fairness and reliability.

item.title: Evaluation finds AI models often ignore architecture rules, with Opus failing compliance about 60% of the time [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: An evaluation of various AI models revealed that many frequently disregard architectural rules, with the Opus model failing to comply about 60% of the time. This assessment underscores ongoing difficulties in ensuring AI systems consistently adhere to established structural guidelines. The findings highlight the challenge of aligning AI behavior with predefined architecture standards, which is critical for reliable and predictable AI system design. This issue may affect the deployment and trustworthiness of AI applications that rely on strict architectural compliance.

item.title: CorpusIQ explains AI intelligence layer as a query-driven system integrating multiple business data sources for real-time, cross-domain answers without data movement or pre-defined schemas [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: CorpusIQ describes an AI intelligence layer as a query-driven system that integrates multiple business data sources to provide real-time, cross-domain answers without moving data or requiring predefined schemas. This layer acts as an intermediary between AI assistants and various business systems, enabling users to ask plain-English questions and receive validated, source-cited responses by reading relevant data in parallel. Unlike connector platforms, ETL pipelines, business intelligence tools, or generic MCP servers, the intelligence layer does not move or transform data, nor does it rely on pre-configured queries or dashboards. Instead, it dynamically identifies and accesses the necessary data sources at query time, supporting complex questions that span multiple domains and improving decision-making efficiency without the need for extensive engineering resources or data duplication.

item.title: Democrats and Republicans express shared concerns about AI risks and the need for responsible regulation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Both Democratic and Republican lawmakers have voiced concerns about the risks associated with artificial intelligence, highlighting a bipartisan consensus on the importance of responsible AI regulation. Despite their political differences, members from both parties agree on the need to carefully address the challenges posed by AI technologies. This shared stance underscores a growing recognition of AI's potential impact and the necessity for thoughtful oversight to manage its development and deployment.

item.title: Ford executives say replacing human engineers with AI was a mistake, rehiring 350 veteran engineers to improve vehicle quality and prevent defects [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Ford has acknowledged that replacing experienced human engineers with artificial intelligence in certain engineering processes was a mistake. The company rehired about 350 veteran engineers to mentor younger staff and reprogram AI diagnostic tools, aiming to improve vehicle quality and prevent defects. This move has contributed to Ford's rise to the top position among mainstream brands in the latest JD Power Quality Survey. The rehired engineers now lead efforts to troubleshoot vehicles and refine automated systems to catch potential failures before production, helping Ford avoid costly recalls. The company's experience highlights the limitations of AI when used without sufficient human oversight, especially in complex tasks requiring deep expertise. This case reflects a broader trend where companies that relied heavily on AI-driven layoffs have had to rehire many employees to maintain quality and customer satisfaction.

item.title: Researchers present an iterative data generation pipeline to detect and control sycophancy in language models using cascading linear features for improved interpretability and steering [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an iterative data generation pipeline that improves the detection and control of sycophancy in language models by isolating cascading linear features linked to this behavior. This approach moves beyond simple binary sample pairs to identify samples exhibiting varying degrees of features that scale linearly with sycophantic behavior, enabling better feature disentanglement and interpretability. The method demonstrates that sycophancy-related features form linearly separable subspaces, allowing for more precise selection of model activations corresponding to the behavior compared to baseline techniques. The study evaluates the pipeline's effectiveness in detecting, scoring, and steering language models away from sycophancy, finding that it matches or outperforms existing methods such as LLM-as-a-judge and system prompting while requiring less computational effort. This work offers enhanced interpretability guarantees and provides code and data to support further research in controlling undesirable model behaviors.

item.title: Researchers present CORE-Bench v1.1 and OOD suite to evaluate AI agent performance beyond accuracy saturation, highlighting efficiency, reliability, and human-agent collaboration benefits [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CORE-Bench v1.1 and an out-of-distribution (OOD) task suite to evaluate AI agent performance beyond traditional accuracy metrics. Using the CORE-Bench Hard benchmark for computational reproducibility of scientific code, they highlight six key performance dimensions often overlooked after accuracy saturation: construct validity, out-of-distribution generalizability, efficiency, reliability, the relative impact of model versus scaffold, and benefits from human-agent collaboration. Their findings demonstrate that even when accuracy plateaus, these benchmarks provide valuable insights into agent capabilities. The study identifies previously unrecognized threats to construct validity in CORE-Bench Hard and presents improved evaluation tools with CORE-Bench v1.1 and CORE-Bench OOD. Additionally, a randomized experiment showed that human-agent collaboration can significantly speed up reproducibility tasks, roughly doubling efficiency compared to human-only efforts. This work advocates for a more comprehensive and rigorous evaluation framework that moves beyond accuracy-centric approaches in assessing AI agents.

item.title: Researchers find refusal behavior in instruction-tuned chat models is gated downstream of persona expression, with compliant persona suppressing refusal in Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have discovered that in instruction-tuned chat models like Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, refusal behavior is influenced by the model's persona expression. Specifically, a compliant persona suppresses refusal responses, with experiments showing refusal rates dropping significantly when the compliant persona direction is activated. The study reveals that refusal is gated downstream of persona expression, occurring at later layers in the model's activation space rather than being an isolated mechanism. The team extracted distinct directions in the models' activation space corresponding to compliant persona and refusal traits and manipulated these to observe their interaction. Reintroducing the refusal direction restored refusal behavior only at late layers, and removing the persona direction at these layers returned refusal rates to baseline, confirming that refusal depends on persona expression at a late stage. This finding challenges previous approaches that treated refusal as independent, highlighting the importance of considering persona in understanding refusal mechanisms in chat models.

item.title: Researchers present AlgoEvolve, an LLM-driven evolutionary framework that generates and improves Python-based algorithmic trading strategies with meta-evolutionary prompt optimization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AlgoEvolve, a novel framework that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate and iteratively improve Python-based algorithmic trading strategies. This system applies evolutionary principles to create executable trading programs that adapt to changing market conditions, demonstrating autonomous shifts in trading rules across various experiments. AlgoEvolve also incorporates a meta-evolutionary process that optimizes the prompts guiding program synthesis, enhancing search heuristics to balance exploration and exploitation while reducing failures. The framework addresses the challenges of algorithmic trading, such as noise and non-stationarity, by rigorously testing strategies and evolving both the programs and the instructions that generate them. The meta-evolutionary outer loop consistently outperforms initial human-designed prompts, indicating that LLM-driven semantic evolution is a promising approach for continuous program synthesis in complex, dynamic environments.

item.title: Researchers introduce an LLM-powered pipeline for comparative governance analysis of DAO and corporate AI protocols, analyzing 4,323 records to study participation and thematic convergence in 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a large language model (LLM)-powered pipeline to analyze governance structures of AI agent protocols, focusing on their interoperability standards. The study compares two governance models-ERC-8004, a permissionless on-chain standard, and Google A2A, a corporate-led standard-by examining 4,323 governance participation records to understand how institutional design influences thematic priorities and community dynamics. Using automated annotation, neural topic modeling, and multi-layer network analysis, the researchers found that while governance forms affect substantive focus, both models show similar levels of participation inequality and community fragmentation. Notably, the permissionless governance setting exhibited denser discourse alignment, suggesting that open governance may encourage greater thematic convergence despite decentralized participation. The study highlights the potential of LLM-assisted methods to advance empirical research on technology governance and inform the design of more equitable AI standards. All data and code from the study are publicly available.

item.title: Researchers develop provenance-aware AI framework integrating Reddit, WebMD, and FDA data to unify psychiatric medication safety information with traceable claims and early adverse event detection [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a provenance-aware, knowledge-graph-based AI framework that integrates data from Reddit, WebMD, and the U.S. FDA Adverse Event Reporting System to unify psychiatric medication safety information. This system processes over 466,000 Reddit posts, 60,000 WebMD reviews, and two decades of FDA records for nine antidepressants, enabling traceable claims and distinguishing between regulatory facts and patient experiences. The framework uses advanced entity recognition with high accuracy and reveals that patient-generated data provide an independent safety signal, often identifying adverse events earlier than official reports.

item.title: Researchers propose Drift-Diffusion-Enhanced Elo system to accelerate chess skill assessment using move-level data, demonstrating faster adaptation to skill changes than traditional Elo [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Drift-Diffusion-Enhanced Elo Rating System (DD-Elo), a new approach to assessing chess skill that incorporates move-level data to provide faster and more responsive updates than the traditional Elo system. Inspired by cognitive neuroscience models, DD-Elo treats skill expression as a decision-making process, allowing it to capture rapid changes in player ability while maintaining theoretical consistency with existing ratings. The system addresses the limitations of conventional Elo ratings, which rely solely on match outcomes and thus respond slowly to shifts in player performance. Through rigorous mathematical analysis and extensive experiments, the researchers demonstrated that DD-Elo adapts more quickly to skill fluctuations without sacrificing accuracy. This method offers a backward-compatible and explainable enhancement for chess rating systems, with implementation code made publicly available for further use and development.

item.title: Researchers propose institutional attestation as a governance model for autonomous AI systems to control high-risk actions with independent verification and tamper-evident logs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed a new governance model for autonomous AI systems that perform high-risk actions, such as clinical prescribing and software deployment. The model, called institutional attestation, allows AI agents to maintain autonomy in planning and reasoning but restricts their authority to execute critical actions without independent verification. Execution depends on preconditions attested by separate authoritative sources, cryptographically linked to the AI's declared intent, and evaluated by a deterministic policy, with all decisions recorded in tamper-evident logs for independent review. This approach formalizes how human institutions govern powerful autonomous actors by focusing on attested evidence at the point of action rather than monitoring internal reasoning. The researchers demonstrated a proof-of-concept implementation and illustrated the model's application in scenarios like software deployment and clinical prescribing, highlighting its potential to enhance safety and accountability in autonomous AI operations.

item.title: Researchers present COrigami, an AI pipeline generating flat-foldable, visually recognizable origami crease patterns from natural language using reinforcement learning and algorithmic optimization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed COrigami, an AI-driven pipeline that generates flat-foldable origami crease patterns from natural language descriptions. The system combines semantic interpretation, geometric computation, and reinforcement learning to produce crease patterns that meet strict mathematical constraints while maintaining visual recognizability. COrigami serves as a collaborative tool, providing structural designs that human artists can further refine. The pipeline involves creating a semantic stick figure, computing base packing, solving for flat-foldability, shaping the crease pattern, and refining the model through an autonomous aesthetic evaluation loop. By integrating algorithmic optimization with aesthetic critique, the approach addresses the challenge of balancing physical constraints and artistic design in computational origami. This work demonstrates how AI can support co-creativity in domains requiring multi-objective optimization, enabling reliable and mathematically grounded design assistance for physical art forms like origami.

item.title: Researchers find verifying coding agent rewards is harder than generating solutions due to underspecified intent and reward hacking, requiring co-evolving verification methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that for modern coding agents, verifying solutions is more challenging than generating them due to the inherent difficulty of capturing human intent accurately. Verification relies on proxies for intent, which are often underspecified and can lead to issues like reward hacking during model training. This shifts the traditional view that verification is easier than creation, highlighting the complexity of ensuring solutions meet intended goals. The study evaluates verification signals based on scalability, faithfulness, and robustness, examining four types of reward mechanisms across various coding tasks. Experiments demonstrate that carefully designed verification methods can reduce reward hacking and improve task outcomes, but no single fixed reward function remains effective as agent capabilities advance. The findings emphasize the need for verification approaches to evolve alongside solution generators to maintain reliability and effectiveness.

item.title: arXiv: Empirical study evaluates tool-augmented LLM agents on 243 real-world energy market analytics tasks using live data and domain-specific tools [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new empirical study evaluates the performance of tool-augmented large language model (LLM) agents on 243 real-world energy market analytics tasks. These tasks span market data retrieval, knowledge interpretation, and advanced quantitative modeling, requiring live data access and specialized domain knowledge. The study compares closed-source and open-source LLMs equipped with domain-specific tools such as electricity market APIs, regulatory databases, and optimization models, assessing their responses through a multi-dimensional evaluation protocol. The evaluation environment includes expert-curated problems covering price and demand analysis, tariff impact modeling, asset revenue estimation, hedging strategies, and optimization, with varying difficulty levels. The study highlights the interaction between model capabilities and domain tooling in a complex professional setting and publicly releases key artifacts to support reproducibility and further research.

item.title: arXiv paper identifies gaps in multimodal large language model evaluation, highlighting issues like temporal-spatial coherence and multimodal consistency [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent paper on arXiv highlights significant gaps in the evaluation of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), which process inputs like text, images, audio, and video to generate responses. The study points out that current benchmarks focus on isolated tasks and fail to assess how well these models integrate information across different modalities. Key areas needing better evaluation include temporal-spatial coherence, understanding of the physical world, multimodal consistency, and selective attention. The authors review existing evaluation methods and benchmark taxonomies, emphasizing that addressing these shortcomings is crucial for accurately measuring progress in multimodal intelligence. Improving evaluation frameworks will help reveal the true capabilities and limitations of MLLMs, guiding future research and development in this rapidly advancing field.

item.title: Researchers introduce OpenFinGym, a unified multi-task gym environment for evaluating quantitative finance agents across forecasting, trading, risk management, and fraud detection [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed OpenFinGym, a unified gym environment designed to evaluate quantitative finance agents across multiple interrelated tasks including forecasting, market generation, real-time trading, and fraud detection. This platform addresses the limitations of existing tools that focus on isolated tasks, potentially overstating agent capabilities and overlooking challenges in generalization and real-market decision-making. OpenFinGym features an automated task-construction pipeline that converts quantitative finance research into executable tasks, a containerized runtime with verification services to prevent data leakage, and a low-latency paper trading engine. It also supports long-horizon and event-driven forecasts and integrates with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning methods, providing a comprehensive framework for developing and testing finance agents in realistic, multi-stage workflows.

item.title: Researchers identify compositional behavioral leakage causing cross-module interference in prompt-composed agentic systems, demonstrated on Claude Sonnet 4.6 with a new evaluation protocol [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a phenomenon called compositional behavioral leakage (CBL) in prompt-composed agentic systems, where modifying one prompt module unintentionally alters the behavior of others despite no direct dependencies. This interference arises from the architectural design of transformers, which lack formal boundaries between concatenated modules. The team demonstrated CBL on the Claude Sonnet 4.6 agent using a novel three-channel evaluation protocol that perturbs non-focal modules by volume, content, and form, finding that only content changes produced measurable effects without flipping recommendations, indicating subtle but cumulative impacts on agent decisions. The study distinguishes CBL from other known failure modes such as adversarial attacks or privacy leaks and provides an operational definition, a reusable testing protocol, and a set of falsifiable predictions. These contributions establish cross-module interference measurement as an essential component for evaluating prompt-composed agents, highlighting the need for more rigorous assessment methods to ensure reliable agent behavior in complex modular systems.

item.title: arXiv paper presents a mathematical interpretation of Kurzweil's accelerating returns thesis and proposes the Qualitative Engine for Science to address limits in AI-driven scientific discovery [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new paper on arXiv offers a mathematical interpretation of Ray Kurzweil's accelerating returns thesis, which suggests that technological progress in fields like computing, AI, brain science, and biotechnology is self-reinforcing and exponential. The paper argues that while this acceleration enhances executional and infrastructural capabilities, it does not fully address the core challenge of scientific discovery, which requires qualitative reasoning to identify when existing frameworks are inadequate and to determine the next conceptual steps. The authors highlight recent AI benchmark results showing a significant gap between human flexible reasoning and current AI performance, emphasizing the need for systems that support qualitative scientific insight. They propose the Qualitative Engine for Science (QES) as a tool to complement accelerating quantitative capabilities by preserving and organizing the human wisdom involved in scientific discovery. This approach underscores that the value of such tools extends beyond the timeline for achieving artificial general intelligence, focusing instead on sustaining meaningful human understanding in science.

item.title: Researchers introduce Narration-of-Thought, a system prompt that improves ethical reasoning in large language models by reducing stakeholder collapse and uncertainty suppression without additional training [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Narration-of-Thought (NoT), a system prompt designed to enhance ethical reasoning in large language models by addressing two common issues: stakeholder collapse and uncertainty suppression. NoT structures the reasoning process into five distinct sections-protagonist, stakeholders, two-step consequences, uncertainty, and commitment-without requiring additional training or fine-tuning. Testing on 100 moral dilemma scenarios across multiple models showed that NoT significantly reduces stakeholder collapse from up to 31% to under 1% and uncertainty suppression from up to 72% to between 1% and 24%. The study demonstrated that NoT's improvements are not due to increased token usage but stem from its structured approach, with each section contributing to better ethical reasoning. Further enhancements were achieved through textual-gradient descent, and a multi-stakeholder debate protocol using NoT led to near-complete consensus in ethical judgments. This method provides transparent reasoning traces that clarify stakeholders, consequences, and uncertainties, offering a reliable foundation for deploying ethical AI agents.

item.title: Researchers propose Geometry-Aware Monte Carlo Tree Search to solve extremal combinatorial geometry problems, achieving new best-known results on five of six tested problems including Max-N3IL and Smallest Complete Set [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a Geometry-Aware Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) framework to address extremal problems in combinatorial geometry involving point configurations on an $n \times n$ grid with strict geometric constraints. This approach improves upon classical solvers and standard machine learning models by incrementally updating feasible actions and enforcing constraints more efficiently, notably reducing complexity in problems like the No-Three-in-Line (Max-N3IL). The method also leverages geometric symmetries to enhance search efficiency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this framework achieves new best-known results on five out of six tested problems, including finding larger configurations for Max-N3IL and tighter upper bounds for the Smallest Complete Set problem. These findings establish Geometry-Aware MCTS as a versatile tool for discovering novel configurations in combinatorial geometry.

item.title: Researchers propose an agentic aggregator framework for electric bus fleet operations integrating scheduling optimization and supervisory agents to manage pricing, disturbances, and vehicle-to-grid flexibility [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an agentic aggregator framework to enhance the operation of electric bus fleets by integrating an optimization-based scheduling model with supervisory agents that manage disturbances, pricing adaptations, and schedule evaluations. This framework coordinates complex factors such as service reliability, battery charge, charger availability, electricity prices, route energy uncertainty, and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) interactions to maintain feasible schedules and improve flexibility use. A case study of a realistic depot scenario tested the framework's performance under various conditions, including service delays, energy deviations, and price shocks, using both profit-based and operation-based coordination modes. The results demonstrated that the agentic system can selectively trigger real-time re-optimization and support adaptive fleet-grid coordination, though it also highlighted a trade-off where profit-oriented configurations might extract value from public transport operators. These findings suggest that while agentic aggregators offer promising tools for managing electric bus V2G operations, their implementation in public fleet contexts requires transparent coordination, auditable pricing mechanisms, and clear value-sharing policies to ensure equitable and effective deployment.

item.title: Researchers propose a lattice-theoretic method to create unbiased, self-consistent set-valued oracles for AI probability estimates, addressing self-reference problems in future event prediction [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed a lattice-theoretic approach to address the self-reference problem faced by non-agentic "oracle" AI systems that estimate probabilities of future events. These systems can alter the probabilities they predict once their answers are known and acted upon. Instead of providing a single probability, the proposed method outputs a credal set that is unbiased and self-consistent with the consequences of being learned, using the Knaster--Tarski fixed-point theorem to identify a canonical, nontrivial solution. The approach ensures existence, self-consistency, and nonemptiness of the solution and reduces to classical point estimates for non-performative questions. For binary events, the canonical answer forms an interval under certain assumptions. This lattice-theoretic framework generalizes from binary events to arbitrary random variables, replacing conditional probabilities with conditional laws. The study concludes with open questions about the broader applicability of the interval characterization in this generalized setting.

item.title: Researchers evaluate confidence interval methods for classifier performance metrics in text classification with small samples and nested data, proposing improved approaches for large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have evaluated various confidence interval methods for classifier performance metrics in text classification, particularly under conditions common in social science research such as small sample sizes, infrequent constructs, and nested data structures. They found that commonly used methods like the Wald interval and basic percentile bootstrap often provide inaccurate uncertainty estimates, especially when datasets are small or classifier performance is high. The study highlights improved accuracy using methods such as Agresti-Coull, Wilson, Clopper-Pearson, and a novel pseudo-count regularized bootstrap, especially for F1 score calculations. The research also addresses the challenge of texts nested within individuals, demonstrating that adjustments for effective sample size and degrees of freedom are necessary for accurate interval estimation. Among bootstrap approaches, the hierarchical bootstrap performs better than the cluster bootstrap when individuals contribute a moderate number of texts but tends to be overly conservative with fewer texts per individual. By offering guidance on appropriate confidence interval estimation, the study aims to enhance transparency in machine learning applications and encourage careful consideration of validation sample sizes during study design.

item.title: Researchers show supervised machine learning cannot achieve symbolic-level syllogistic reasoning due to data and training limitations, with experiments on Euler Net and GPT-5 models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that supervised machine learning systems face fundamental limitations in achieving symbolic-level syllogistic reasoning, even with increased training data and time. Their study identifies two key methodological barriers: training data cannot differentiate all 24 valid types of syllogistic reasoning, and the end-to-end learning approach creates conflicting objectives between pattern recognition and logical reasoning components. Experimental results show that models like Euler Net fail to perform rigorous syllogistic reasoning, and while advanced models such as GPT-5 can reach high accuracy on certain reasoning tasks, they may still produce incorrect explanations. The research further reveals that the form of input-whether words, repeated words, simple symbols, or random symbols-significantly affects reasoning performance. Despite achieving apparent accuracy, supervised learning models stop training early and do not attain the strict logical rigor characteristic of symbolic reasoning. These findings suggest inherent constraints in data-driven machine learning approaches for complex logical tasks, highlighting a gap between current AI capabilities and true symbolic reasoning.

item.title: Researchers introduce MKG-RAG-Bench, a cross-domain benchmark for evaluating retrieval in multimodal knowledge graph-augmented generation using general and medical datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MKG-RAG-Bench, a new cross-domain benchmark designed to evaluate retrieval in multimodal knowledge graph-augmented generation (MKG-RAG). This benchmark addresses the challenges of retrieving heterogeneous and multimodal knowledge, which is critical for grounding large language models but often overlooked by existing benchmarks. MKG-RAG-Bench includes datasets from general and medical domains with aligned question-answering tasks to assess both retrieval and downstream generation performance. The benchmark was developed using a large language model-based curation pipeline that filters low-utility knowledge and generates structurally grounded queries with exact supervision. Experiments across various retriever types and modality settings demonstrate that effective multimodal retrieval remains a significant challenge and strongly influences the quality of generated outputs. By focusing on retrieval as a primary evaluation target, MKG-RAG-Bench provides a foundation for diagnosing current limitations and advancing the development of MKG-RAG systems.

item.title: Researchers present auto-psych, an agent-based system automating theory discovery and experimentation in computational cognitive science using crowdsourced human data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed auto-psych, an agent-based system that automates theory discovery and experimentation in computational cognitive science by independently collecting human data through crowdsourced surveys. The system uses nested loops where one generates and critiques cognitive models while the other designs and conducts experiments online, enabling rapid and reliable theory testing. Tested on a classic cognitive psychology problem involving perceptions of randomness in coin flip sequences, auto-psych produced theories that fit human data better than existing scientific models. The system's design allows it to recover known theories from synthetic data and improve upon them through systematic experimentation. By leveraging crowdsourcing platforms for scalable data collection and representing theories as code, auto-psych demonstrates the potential for AI-driven automation in psychological research. This approach could accelerate scientific discovery by integrating hypothesis generation, experimental design, data collection, and analysis into a unified automated workflow.

item.title: Researchers propose Clinical Harness architecture for governable AI skills in medical care, demonstrating lifecycle osteoporosis management under runtime governance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced the Clinical Harness, a runtime governance framework designed to manage AI-driven clinical capabilities that operate continuously over time. This architecture supports the registration, orchestration, protection, and monitoring of AI skills in medical care, addressing the limitations of isolated AI models. Using osteoporosis management as a case study, the team demonstrates how integrating knowledge-driven, data-driven, and physics-enhanced AI skills can facilitate comprehensive lifecycle care under active governance.

item.title: Researchers find large reasoning models spend more time on incorrect problems while humans spend less, revealing opposite deliberation allocation despite similar difficulty tracking [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that large reasoning models (LRMs) and humans exhibit opposite patterns in how they allocate time when solving problems. While both spend more time on harder problems overall, LRMs tend to spend more time on problems they answer incorrectly, whereas humans spend less time on their incorrect attempts. This study distinguishes between two aspects of deliberation: how response time correlates with difficulty across different problems and how time is allocated between successes and failures on the same problem. The analysis, conducted on a dataset comparing human and LRM performance, shows that although both humans and LRMs similarly track problem difficulty across items, they differ significantly in their within-item time allocation. Humans appear to disengage from problems they expect to fail, while LRMs continue deliberating longer when uncertain, which often leads to failure. This divergence suggests that LRMs and humans use different stopping policies despite sharing a common difficulty signal, highlighting contrasting approaches to problem-solving and metareasoning.

item.title: arXiv: NeuraDock releases open-source EEG agent tutorial for real-time visual cognitive load analysis using quality-gated Alpha dynamics workflow [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: NeuraDock has released an open-source EEG agent tutorial that guides users through a quality-gated workflow for analyzing Alpha dynamics and visual cognitive load in real time. The tutorial enables researchers and developers to install the agent, perform EEG preprocessing and quality control, generate Alpha activity figures, compare cognitive load between rest and task conditions, and utilize a real-time API with an interpretation layer for quality risk assessment. This approach bridges the gap between offline EEG analysis and real-time cognitive load monitoring by integrating acquisition, custom quality control, feature extraction, and web API components. The tutorial includes validation using a public mini-dataset, where the agent processed 18 recordings and produced within-subject comparisons showing task-related posterior Alpha suppression in most cases. It also benchmarks online API latency and demonstrates initial evidence of repeatability in cognitive load measures. Designed for applied teams, the tutorial offers a transparent and reproducible path from raw EEG data to real-time visual cognitive load prototypes.

item.title: Researchers present NeuraDock Agent, an open-source architecture combining a deterministic EEG engine with a hardware-aware language layer for low-channel EEG analysis and boundary-aware context grounding [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed NeuraDock Agent, an open-source system designed to improve low-channel electroencephalography (EEG) analysis by combining a deterministic local EEG processing engine with a hardware-aware language model layer. This architecture ensures that the language model receives only curated, context-specific summaries about the EEG hardware, workflows, and scientific boundaries, while raw data remains local. The system aims to prevent unsupported interpretations common in sparse EEG data by grounding analysis within known hardware and implementation limits. The NeuraDock Agent was evaluated through multiple tests, including repeated numerical analyses of EEG recordings, robustness checks under data transmission failures, and boundary-awareness benchmarks involving various question types and language models. These evaluations demonstrated consistent results and effective handling of data boundaries, supporting the approach as a practical method for calibrating EEG data interpretation. However, the researchers note that these findings do not establish clinical validity or a definitive cognitive-load index.

item.title: Researchers develop a framework for radical AI interpretability to infer AI systems' beliefs and desires from computational data, addressing safety and trust challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new framework for interpreting AI systems as agents by combining the philosophical approach of radical interpretation with mechanistic interpretability techniques. This framework aims to determine an AI system's beliefs, desires, and meanings based on its computational data, addressing critical safety concerns such as understanding AI goals and detecting deception. The work proposes criteria for evaluating interpretability tools and emphasizes that beliefs and desires must be assessed holistically rather than piecemeal to avoid distortions. The framework highlights that AI systems may not share human concepts, making interpretation challenging but also providing constraints that help in attributing attitudes and propositional structures. By jointly analyzing these elements, the approach offers a more reliable method for reading AI internals, which is essential for building trust and ensuring the safe deployment of AI technologies.

item.title: Researchers introduce PMDformer, a transformer model using patch-mean decoupling and specialized attention mechanisms to improve long-term time series forecasting accuracy and stability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed PMDformer, a transformer-based model designed to improve long-term time series forecasting by addressing challenges in capturing shape similarities across patches and variables. The model introduces patch-mean decoupling (PMD) to separate trend and residual shape information, ensuring the attention mechanism focuses on true shape similarities. Additionally, PMDformer incorporates Trend Restoration Attention (TRA) and Proximal Variable Attention (PVA) to better model long-range dependencies and cross-variable relationships. PMDformer reintegrates decoupled trends during attention calculation and emphasizes recent, relevant time segments to prevent overfitting on outdated correlations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PMDformer outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and stability across multiple long-term forecasting benchmarks. The model's code is publicly available for further research and application.

item.title: Researchers develop explainable ensemble machine learning models to detect cirrhosis in hepatitis C patients with up to 96.92% accuracy using data from 2038 Egyptian patients [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed explainable ensemble machine learning models to detect cirrhosis in hepatitis C patients with high accuracy, using data from 2,038 Egyptian patients. The study trained four algorithms-Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Machine, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and Extra Trees-on a dataset with 28 attributes, finding that the Extra Trees model performed best with an accuracy of 96.92%, recall of 94.00%, and precision of 99.81% using only 16 features. Cirrhosis, a severe liver scarring condition caused by long-term hepatitis C infection, often progresses silently before leading to liver failure and other complications. Early detection is critical to prevent disease progression, and this research demonstrates the potential of machine learning to provide precise diagnostic support for cirrhosis in hepatitis C patients, a task not previously addressed by ML studies.

item.title: Researchers propose EvoOptiGraph, a graph-based coevolution framework that improves large language models for optimization modeling by generating structurally diverse mixed-integer linear programs and targeting model weaknesses [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced EvoOptiGraph, a novel framework designed to enhance large language models (LLMs) for automating optimization modeling from natural language. EvoOptiGraph addresses key challenges such as limited structural diversity in training data and static data generation by representing mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs) as attributed bipartite graphs and applying evolutionary operators to create diverse instances. This approach enables a co-evolution of data and model, where weaknesses identified in the model guide the generation of new training examples, forming a continuous improvement loop. The training process involves supervised fine-tuning on an initial dataset followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, using graph-derived signals to target model failures. Empirical tests on six public datasets demonstrate that EvoOptiGraph outperforms larger generalist models and specialized baselines in accuracy, executability, and generalization. These results highlight the effectiveness of targeted data-model coevolution in improving LLM performance on optimization modeling tasks.

item.title: Researchers propose a multi-level validation and traceability framework to improve reliability and executability of AI-generated telescope scheduling decisions [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a multi-level validation and traceability framework to enhance the reliability and executability of AI-generated telescope scheduling decisions. This framework systematically verifies AI outputs before execution, addressing issues such as inconsistent data references, reasoning errors, and non-executable decisions that limit AI's use in high-reliability astronomical observations. It incorporates data validation, logical consistency checks, and constraint verification to filter and correct invalid decisions while explicitly representing the reasoning process for traceability.

item.title: Researchers develop a smart email dispatcher using large language models to automatically route emails to relevant WhatsApp groups in an engineering college, improving productivity and reducing cognitive load [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a smart email dispatcher that uses large language models (LLMs) to automatically analyze and route emails to relevant WhatsApp groups within an engineering college. This system aims to streamline communication by directing emails to appropriate student groups based on content, reducing the manual effort and errors associated with forwarding messages across platforms. The approach enhances productivity and lowers the cognitive load involved in managing large volumes of email communication. The dispatcher operates through an agent framework that inputs email content along with instructions and context into LLMs, which then determine the correct recipient groups without relying on labeled datasets. By automating the distribution of information, the system facilitates timely and accurate communication among students across different semesters and programs, improving organizational efficiency.

item.title: Researchers present LLM-based methodology combining fine-tuned models and human oversight to detect emerging service quality topics and inequities in multilingual public sector feedback [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new methodology that combines fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) with human oversight to analyze multilingual public sector service feedback. This approach aims to detect emerging service quality issues and potential inequities, particularly in tax administrations where fair service delivery is crucial for trust and compliance. The framework integrates statistical techniques and human-AI collaboration to provide accurate, efficient, and context-aware analysis of growing volumes of textual feedback. The methodology was tested using similarity analysis and evaluations by experienced tax officers, showing better alignment with expert judgments than existing models. By incorporating a human-in-the-loop system, the approach reduces errors commonly associated with LLMs and enhances the reliability of insights. This work supports scalable, evidence-based decision-making and contributes to responsible AI development that improves service quality, fairness, and public trust through more effective feedback analysis.

item.title: Researchers present an LLM-based pipeline to autoformalize agent prompts and policy documents into verified Cedar Policy Language code, improving coverage on MedAgentBench over prior symbolic methods [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an automated pipeline that uses large language models (LLMs) to convert agent prompts, tool descriptions, and natural language policy documents into formally verified policies written in the Cedar Policy Language. This approach addresses the limitations of existing methods that either rely on probabilistic guardrails without formal guarantees or on hand-coded symbolic enforcement that lacks scalability. The new pipeline demonstrated improved coverage of natural-language policy specifications on the MedAgentBench benchmark compared to prior symbolic methods. The system employs a generator-critic loop powered by LLMs to ensure the accuracy and formal verification of the generated policies. By automating the formalization process, the pipeline can handle a broader range of real-world policy specifications, enhancing agent safety in high-stakes domains where strict policy enforcement is critical.

item.title: Researchers introduce SkillDisCo framework to distill and compile reusable procedural skills from agent task traces, improving success rates and efficiency in FSM-defined scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SkillDisCo, a framework that distills and compiles reusable procedural skills from agent task traces to improve efficiency and success rates in finite state machine (FSM)-defined scenarios. By viewing successful task executions as paths in an unknown transition graph, SkillDisCo identifies reusable parameterized control-flow subgraphs and compiles them into callable, executable, and verifiable skills. Experiments on platforms like ALFWorld and WebArena demonstrate that SkillDisCo enhances performance by reducing the number of agent turns and increasing success across various benchmarks and model scales. This approach addresses the challenge of agents repeatedly solving similar tasks from scratch, which leads to unnecessary reasoning costs and lengthy execution traces. Prior methods explored workflow reuse but lacked clarity on which scenarios support procedural skills and how to represent shared procedural structures. SkillDisCo's distillation and compilation process captures shared experience as reusable execution structures, offering a systematic way to improve agent task execution efficiency.

item.title: Researchers present NebulaExp-8B, a transparent post-training pipeline with full-scale ablation on Qwen3-8B-base, improving instruction and reasoning benchmarks using supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced NebulaExp-8B, a transparent post-training pipeline designed to enhance large language models' instruction-following and reasoning abilities. Built on the Qwen3-8B-base model, NebulaExp-8B employs a comprehensive data processing approach and combines supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning to improve performance on various benchmarks. The pipeline includes two specialized branches: one for general instruction tasks and another focused on complex reasoning. The team curated a large dataset of 3.84 million supervised fine-tuning samples and a 200,000-sample reinforcement learning candidate pool, applying techniques such as response distillation, multi-dimensional filtering, and difficulty grading. Their optimized supervised fine-tuning method raised benchmark scores significantly, with further gains achieved through reinforcement learning. Additionally, they explored single-teacher and multi-teacher preference distillation methods to reduce reliance on task verifiers, demonstrating notable improvements with fewer samples. This work offers a fully reproducible empirical recipe for post-training 8B-scale language models and provides detailed analysis of trade-offs among instruction adherence, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and general knowledge capabilities.

item.title: Researchers introduce LeanGuard, a lightweight safety guardrail model that matches reasoning-based moderation accuracy with 100x less compute and improved robustness on public benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed LeanGuard, a lightweight safety guardrail model that achieves moderation accuracy comparable to reasoning-based methods while using approximately 100 times less computational power. LeanGuard employs a 395 million parameter label-only encoder that processes inputs in a single forward pass, contrasting with heavier models that generate chain-of-thought reasoning before making decisions. This approach challenges the assumption that step-by-step reasoning is necessary for effective moderation. The study involved training both a lightweight bidirectional encoder and a reasoning guard on the same dataset, then removing the reasoning component to isolate its impact. Results showed that LeanGuard matched the performance of larger reasoning models on public benchmarks, maintaining robustness even under noisy training labels and achieving higher recall at strict false-positive rates. These findings suggest that current moderation benchmarks may not sufficiently reward reasoning, and the necessity of chain-of-thought reasoning in safety guardrails remains unproven. The researchers have made all source code and models, including LeanGuard, publicly available.

item.title: Researchers propose Kalman Prototypical Networks for few-shot fault detection in combined cycle gas turbines, improving accuracy and stability on simulated leak fault tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Kalman Prototypical Network (KPN), a few-shot learning framework designed to improve fault detection in combined-cycle gas turbines (CCGTs), which are critical for efficient and environmentally friendly power generation. The KPN models class prototype evolution as latent stochastic states within a dynamic system, enhancing robustness and reducing variance in fault diagnosis despite limited labeled data. Testing on synthetic datasets simulating normal and leak fault conditions demonstrated that KPN outperforms existing few-shot learning methods in accuracy and stability. The study utilized high-fidelity Modelica-based simulations of an offshore CCGT system to generate data under transient conditions, enabling evaluation of the KPN's performance on leak fault detection tasks. Compared to conventional approaches like Matching Networks, Relation Networks, and MAML, KPN showed superior training convergence and generalization by stabilizing class representations. This advancement suggests that KPN is well-suited for real-world applications where fault data are scarce, potentially enhancing maintenance and reliability in power generation systems.

item.title: Researchers present LithoDreamer, a physics-informed World Model framework for multi-stage computational lithography, achieving state-of-the-art performance in forward evolution and inverse planning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed LithoDreamer, a novel physics-informed World Model framework designed to improve multi-stage computational lithography, a critical process in semiconductor manufacturing. LithoDreamer models the entire lithography pipeline as a decision-driven multi-step evolution system, capturing feature changes across stages such as mask optimization, optical imaging, resist exposure, and development. This approach enables more accurate forward evolution and inverse planning compared to existing models. The framework introduces a contrastive variational optimization method that guides the model to generate lithography process evolutions consistent with real physical behavior without requiring continuous supervision. Experiments demonstrate that LithoDreamer achieves state-of-the-art performance, and the researchers have made their lithography dataset publicly available on GitHub to support further development in this area.

item.title: Researchers present a latent ODE model for continuous spatiotemporal cine cardiac MRI analysis, improving heart failure risk prediction in 72,386 UK Biobank participants [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a latent dynamical model that analyzes continuous spatiotemporal cine cardiac MRI data to improve heart failure risk prediction. The model encodes bi-ventricular anatomy and full-cycle heart motion using neural ordinary differential equations and a graph-based mesh autoencoder, enabling anatomically consistent 3D reconstructions. Tested on 72,386 UK Biobank participants without baseline cardiovascular disease, the model enhanced prediction accuracy beyond traditional cardiac markers and risk equations by capturing detailed ventricular motion patterns. The approach integrates a covariate-conditioned prior and a Cox proportional hazards model to assess deviations linked to incident heart failure. Compared to other methods, it achieved superior balance between reconstruction quality, generative realism, and prognostic performance. These findings suggest that continuous full-cycle modeling of ventricular motion offers valuable cardiac phenotypes beyond conventional MRI summaries, though further validation in diverse patient populations is needed before clinical application.

item.title: Researchers introduce AHOIS, a multi-agent AI system using Socratic questioning for autonomous scientific discovery in complex high-dimensional physical systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AHOIS, a multi-agent AI system that uses Socratic questioning to enable autonomous scientific discovery in complex, high-dimensional physical systems. Unlike traditional AI that follows fixed workflows, AHOIS incorporates a physics-critic agent that challenges and refines hypotheses through causal questioning and falsification, allowing it to adapt and improve its understanding based on experimental evidence. The system was tested on a multimode-fibre optical platform characterized by complex wave transformations and environmental variability. Without relying on pre-existing models or classifiers, AHOIS autonomously proposed and validated a novel encoding hypothesis, identified efficient measurement strategies, diagnosed failure modes, and translated existing imaging protocols to new configurations. Its discoveries led to effective measurements and high classification accuracy on standard datasets, demonstrating improved physical consistency and experimental planning through its Socratic interrogation approach. These results mark a significant step toward fully autonomous, evidence-driven scientific discovery systems capable of self-correction and adaptation in complex physical environments, moving beyond mere automation to genuine epistemic autonomy.

item.title: Researchers propose meta-optimization framework using consensus objective aggregation with LLMs to accelerate 3-SAT algorithm discovery, achieving 67x speedup and improved scaling [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a meta-optimization framework that enhances scientific discovery by simultaneously optimizing both the research process and its evaluation criteria. This approach, called consensus objective aggregation, combines multiple objective functions generated by large language models through correlation-weighted voting to create a stable and adaptive evaluation metric. Applying this method to the discovery of algorithms for 3-SAT problems using digital MemComputing machines, the team achieved a significant improvement, reducing the computational scaling from approximately N^{2.51} to N^{1.33} and delivering a 67-fold speedup on the largest problem instances tested. This framework treats scientific discovery as an evolving optimization challenge, where the criteria for success are refined alongside the solutions themselves. By enabling a self-correcting and dynamic evaluation process, the method supports more efficient exploration of complex problem spaces. The researchers suggest that this problem-agnostic approach could broadly accelerate progress across various scientific domains by improving the way discoveries are evaluated and optimized.

item.title: Researchers propose EGG, an expert-guided agent framework for GPU kernel generation achieving 2.13x speedup over PyTorch on KernelBench and real-world workloads [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed EGG, an Expert-Guided Agent Framework designed to automate the generation of high-performance GPU kernels, which are essential for managing the growing computational demands of large language models (LLMs). EGG integrates expert optimization principles into large language models' decision-making processes, structuring kernel generation into two stages: algorithmic structure design and hardware-specific tuning. This approach enables more effective exploration of optimization strategies, resulting in improved kernel performance. The framework employs a stage-aware multi-agent collaboration mechanism to manage context and ensure stable optimization throughout the process. Testing on KernelBench and real-world workloads demonstrated that EGG achieves an average speedup of 2.13 times compared to PyTorch, outperforming existing agent-based and reinforcement learning methods. This advancement could significantly reduce the manual effort required for GPU kernel tuning and enhance the efficiency of LLM computations.

item.title: Researchers introduce ResilPhase, a noise-resilient diffusion acceleration framework using phase mapping and macro-trajectory extrapolation to improve inference speed and fidelity in diffusion models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ResilPhase, a new framework designed to accelerate inference in diffusion models while maintaining high fidelity. This approach addresses the limitations of previous acceleration methods that relied on derivative-based polynomials, which often caused quality degradation due to numerical instability and misaligned extrapolations. ResilPhase reformulates the acceleration process by aligning forecasting with the model's global state evolution and employs a derivative-free extrapolator combined with phase mapping to reduce noise and error growth. The framework replaces intermediate feature prediction with stable macro-trajectory extrapolation in ordinary differential equation space, eliminating feature inconsistency and reducing memory overhead. Experiments on datasets such as FLUX.1-dev and HunyuanVideo demonstrate that ResilPhase achieves state-of-the-art fidelity even under aggressive acceleration ratios, making it a promising solution for improving the efficiency of diffusion-based models.

item.title: Researchers introduce EVAF, a selective parametric consolidation mechanism enhancing memory depth and goal persistence in long-running language agents across GPT-2, TinyLlama, and Mistral-7B [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed EVAF, a selective parametric consolidation mechanism designed to enhance memory depth and goal persistence in long-running language agents. Unlike traditional retrieval systems that fetch past facts at query time, EVAF enables durable goal-conditioned behaviors by selectively consolidating experiences into a small parametric store. This approach was tested using the loop-drift protocol, which challenges agents to maintain goal-directed behavior despite unloading working context and long-loop interference. Evaluations across GPT-2, TinyLlama, and Mistral-7B models showed that while retrieval excels at shallow factual recall, EVAF significantly improves goal persistence and recovery after context unloading with minimal parametric updates. The mechanism operates through two controllable dimensions-selection and actuation-and demonstrates model-dependent write strengths. Additionally, analysis using public Memora event streams highlighted challenges related to stale-memory invalidation, indicating areas for further research. Overall, EVAF provides a complementary form of memory depth distinct from conventional retrieval access, advancing the capabilities of language agents in maintaining long-term goals.

item.title: Researchers propose KARLA method enabling language models to retrieve factual knowledge from knowledge bases during generation, improving accuracy and transparency without retraining [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced KARLA, a method that enables large language models (LLMs) to retrieve factual information from external knowledge bases during text generation. This approach allows the factual content in the model's output to be updated without retraining, improves transparency by linking facts to their sources, and enables smaller models to match the factual accuracy of larger ones. KARLA works by training the model to generate special tokens that trigger queries to the knowledge base, enhancing factual grounding in both short and long-form outputs. Experiments demonstrate that KARLA effectively integrates external knowledge, allowing factual updates through edits to the knowledge base rather than changes to the model's parameters. This method supports explainability and could lead to more reliable and maintainable language models by separating knowledge retrieval from language generation.

item.title: Study analyzes heart rate variability indices in 40 healthy adults using computational methods to assess normality, stability, correlation, reproducibility, and consistency for clinical utility
item.description: A study analyzed heart rate variability (HRV) indices in 40 healthy adults to enhance the clinical utility of HRV measurements. Using computational methods, the research assessed time, frequency, and nonlinear HRV indices for normality, stability, correlation, reproducibility, and consistency. Key findings include that time-domain and nonlinear indices generally follow normal distributions with some gender differences, most indices are stable except those related to high frequency, and certain HF-related indices are highly correlated, suggesting redundancy. The study also compared results with the Fantasia database, finding less than 10% error for most indices except for some in women. Time-domain and nonlinear indices showed low variability across studies, while frequency-domain indices varied more, limiting their use in cross-study comparisons. The researchers identified specific indices-ApEn and IRRR for global variability, HRVi and SD2 for low frequency, and MADRR or rMSSD for high frequency-as most suitable for accurately representing HRV components and improving its relevance in clinical and research settings.

item.title: Researchers introduce Capability Frontier showing benchmarks miss 82% of LLM performance by underestimating multi-model and multi-run capabilities across 21 models and 16 tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced the Capability Frontier, a new evaluation method that reveals existing benchmarks underestimate large language model (LLM) performance by up to 82%. This approach accounts for the combined strengths of multiple models and multiple runs, showing that different models excel at different tasks and that sampling multiple outputs improves overall accuracy. The study analyzed 21 LLMs across 16 diverse benchmarks, demonstrating significant improvements over traditional single-model, single-run evaluations. The Capability Frontier corrects biases from conventional benchmarking by using an oracle to select the best-performing model outputs at each cost level, balancing underestimation from single-model tests and overestimation from noisy samples. Empirical results indicate a 54% reduction in error rates when correcting for single-model evaluation and an 82% improvement when also accounting for multiple runs, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy with 85% less cost. Simulations further show that performance gains increase with the diversity of query topics. These findings suggest that collective LLM capabilities are substantially underestimated in current evaluations, highlighting the need for revised benchmarking practices. This has important implications for deploying LLMs in real-world, multi-domain environments where data heterogeneity is common.

item.title: Researchers propose CASOP framework to synthesize and evaluate over one million context-specific optimization pipelines for warehouse order fulfillment tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Context-Aware Synthesis of Optimization Pipelines (CASOP) framework to address complex decision-making in manual picker-to-goods warehouses, such as item assignment, order batching, and picker routing. CASOP enables the construction and evaluation of over one million context-specific optimization pipelines by integrating a modular algorithm repository, semantic descriptions of warehouse contexts, a taxonomy of order fulfillment problems, and tools for pipeline synthesis and evaluation. This approach helps design and select effective algorithmic solutions tailored to specific warehouse operations. The framework was tested on seven benchmark datasets covering four problem classes, resulting in 1,063,044 valid optimization pipelines. CASOP supports both researchers and practitioners by automating the synthesis of valid and high-performing algorithmic pipelines, overcoming limitations of previous studies that focused on isolated subproblems or fixed algorithm combinations. The open-source software is available for use and further development.

item.title: Researchers introduce LCAi, an AI-assisted life cycle assessment framework using retrieval-augmented generation and big data fusion for improved interpretation and strategic decision-making [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed LCAi, an AI-assisted framework that enhances life cycle assessment (LCA) interpretation by integrating retrieval-augmented generation and big data fusion. This approach addresses the challenge of translating environmental impact data into actionable strategies amid technological, social, and policy uncertainties. The framework uses a multi-perspective retrieval system combined with controlled synthesis to provide evidence-based insights, demonstrated through a case study involving hydrogen-enabled diesel reduction in an Italian apple production facility. The LCAi framework operates in three steps: defining system boundaries and decarbonization targets, executing perspective-specific micro-queries with constrained data retrieval, and synthesizing results neutrally without further retrieval. By incorporating diverse datasets from academia, industry, public discourse, and EU funding, the method mitigates risks of AI hallucination while maintaining cross-domain relevance. This proof-of-concept highlights the potential of advanced AI tools to support strategic decision-making and implementation in LCA studies, especially for scalable technologies.

item.title: arXiv: AgentX introduces a multi-agent system for autonomous self-iteration of industrial recommender systems, automating hypothesis generation, code development, evaluation, and continuous self-improvement [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: AgentX is a multi-agent system designed to automate and accelerate the iteration of industrial recommender systems by autonomously generating hypotheses, developing code, conducting evaluations, and continuously improving itself. This system replaces the traditional human-dependent cycle of idea generation, coding, experimentation, and result analysis with a self-evolving loop that integrates four key stages: brainstorming, development, evaluation, and evolutionary refinement. The Brainstorm Agent creates ranked, executable proposals based on historical data and research, while the Developing Agent converts these proposals into reliable production code. The Evaluation Agent safely rolls out experiments and assesses their outcomes, feeding structured knowledge back into the system. Finally, the Harness Evolution layer refines the agents through semantic-gradient updates, enabling AgentX to improve its own performance over time without manual intervention.

item.title: Researchers introduce TAVR-VLM with Risk-Conditioned Causal Grounding Attention to reduce hallucinations in multimodal AI report generation for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement, achieving 8.1% hallucination rate on 1,482-patient dataset [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed TAVR-VLM, a new multimodal AI framework designed to improve report generation for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) planning by reducing diagnostic hallucinations. The system uses Risk-Conditioned Causal Grounding Attention (R-CGA) to create a structured pathway linking risk assessment to anatomical regions and generated words, enhancing the anatomical grounding of the reports. Evaluated on a dataset of 1,482 patients, TAVR-VLM achieved a significant reduction in hallucination rate to 8.1%, alongside strong performance metrics such as an AUROC of 0.896 and a CIDEr score of 0.936.

item.title: Researchers release a pipeline and dataset generating longitudinal synthetic clinical notes using large language models to support clinical AI development without real patient data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a pipeline and released a dataset that generate synthetic longitudinal clinical notes using large language models, aiming to support the development of clinical AI tools without exposing real patient data.
