This approach addresses privacy concerns by creating synthetic patient records that maintain internal consistency and reflect variations in writing style and clinical detail across a full hospital journey. The pipeline integrates structured patient generation, simulation of patient journeys, and unstructured clinical note creation, enhanced by validation and augmentation steps to improve realism and diversity. The released dataset includes 70 synthetic patients, each with 20 to 50 clinical notes, provided at varying levels of validation to balance realism and scalability for different use cases. This resource facilitates the testing and evaluation of clinical AI systems such as summarization tools, coding models, and decision support systems while avoiding privacy risks associated with real clinical data.

item.title: Researchers propose MO-DiT+HPPO framework for pattern-preserving attribute retrieval using diffusion transformers and metric-ordered sequence training, showing improvements across four attribute domains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MO-DiT+HPPO, a novel framework for pattern-preserving attribute retrieval that combines diffusion transformers with metric-ordered sequence training and hybrid-policy preference optimization. This approach addresses the challenge of retrieving items that both match a target attribute and maintain a fine-grained pattern expressed by a seed set, balancing the trade-off between pattern preservation and attribute relevance. The framework improves retrieval performance across four attribute domains by generating query embeddings for nearest-neighbor search and optimizing the retrieval process through staged training and preference alignment techniques. The MO-DiT+HPPO framework involves raw-sequence pretraining, multi-domain metric-ordered continuation pretraining, tail-centroid fine-tuning, and a hybrid-policy preference optimization step that uses a Pareto pair filter to enhance attribute metrics without compromising pattern purity. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements over pretrained generative retrievers in seven out of eight domain-split scenarios, with detailed analyses confirming the contributions of each component to the overall gains.

item.title: Researchers propose ReTeX framework to recover task-specific expert performance from a single merged multi-task model checkpoint, achieving over 95% accuracy in vision and NLP tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced ReTeX, a framework designed to recover task-specific expert performance from a single merged multi-task model checkpoint. ReTeX addresses the issue of parameter interference in static model merging by predicting additive parameter offsets to undo this interference, enabling recovery of over 95% of individual expert performance in both vision and natural language processing tasks. The framework also includes a router-free task identifier that selects the appropriate expert based on subspace signatures without prior knowledge of task identity. ReTeX improves generalization to unseen tasks by adaptively interpolating expert knowledge, particularly benefiting out-of-distribution scenarios. This approach reduces the need for storing and loading multiple expert components during inference, offering a more efficient solution for multi-task model deployment. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further exploration and application.

item.title: Researchers identify task insensitivity as a key cause of out-of-distribution failures in large language model agents and propose Task-Perturbed NLL Optimization to improve task sensitivity and generalization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified task insensitivity as a major factor contributing to the poor out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization of large language model agents. These models tend to apply learned patterns from training even when faced with similar but distinct tasks, often continuing actions aligned with the original task despite corrupted or altered instructions. This behavior is linked to an attention shift during training away from task instructions toward local observations, indicating an optimization bias toward shortcuts. To address this issue, the researchers propose Task-Perturbed NLL Optimization, a contrastive regularizer designed to enhance the model's sensitivity to task instructions. Evaluations demonstrate that this approach improves task sensitivity and OOD generalization while maintaining stable attention to task tokens, offering a promising direction for developing more adaptable language model agents.

item.title: Researchers analyze chain-of-thought training in large language model agents, finding improvements mainly in prompt action prediction and out-of-domain generalization through selective supervision masking [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have investigated the effects of chain-of-thought (CoT) training on large language model agents, focusing on whether improvements come from enhanced reasoning during action generation or better direct action prediction from prompts. Their study found that while CoT reasoning does not significantly increase the advantage of reasoning-based actions over prompt-based actions, CoT training notably improves the quality of prompt action predictions. Additionally, models at later training stages tend to rely more on prompt information rather than revising actions based on CoT reasoning. The researchers further experimented with selectively masking action-token supervision during training, which led to improved generalization in out-of-domain scenarios. These findings suggest that CoT training primarily enhances prompt-based action prediction and that strategic supervision masking can boost model robustness across different contexts.

item.title: Researchers propose Look-Before-Move framework for narrative-grounded visual attention and camera planning in dynamic 3D story worlds, introducing a new benchmark with 50 stories and 1585 shots [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced the Look-Before-Move framework to enhance camera planning in dynamic 3D story worlds by enabling narrative-grounded visual attention. This approach allows the camera to actively decide what to observe and how to move smoothly while adhering to narrative intent and physical constraints. The framework separates observation specification from motion execution through a Semantic Observation Contract, Monte Carlo Viewpoint Search, and Semantic Trajectory Grounding, improving subject perception, intent consistency, and trajectory quality compared to existing methods. To support this research, the team developed a new dynamic 3D Story World Benchmark based on StoryBlender, which includes 50 stories, 457 scenes, and 1585 shots featuring animated characters and semantic scene configurations. Experiments demonstrate the framework's effectiveness in organizing visual attention before generating camera motion, highlighting its potential for advancing embodied AI and world models in complex 3D environments.

item.title: arXiv: Einstein World Models propose integrating visual-temporal rollouts into LLM reasoning to enhance complex thought beyond text-based methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose Einstein World Models (EWMs), a new framework that integrates visual-temporal rollouts into large language model (LLM) reasoning processes to enhance complex thought beyond text alone. EWMs enable LLMs to generate and inspect short visual simulations of scenarios as hypotheses, supporting reasoning in ways that purely textual methods may not achieve. This approach extends the concept of tool use in LLMs, such as web search or code execution, into the realm of visual thought experiments. The framework involves an LLM calling a specialized world-module to produce these visual rollouts, which are then incorporated into the reasoning trace rather than treated as final answers. By combining language with visual counterfactual reasoning, EWMs aim to improve the ability of AI systems to reason about phenomena beyond direct experience, potentially advancing the capabilities of artificial intelligence in complex problem-solving.

item.title: arXiv: Adaptive Utility-driven Resource Orchestration framework AURORA-AI improves resilience and fairness in AI systems under dynamic conditions, outperforming established controllers in simulations [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: AURORA-AI is a new adaptive resource orchestration framework designed to enhance the resilience and fairness of AI systems operating under dynamic and non-stationary conditions. It integrates advanced control methods and fairness-aware utility metrics to continuously allocate computational resources across diverse AI models, optimizing overall performance, fairness, cost, latency, robustness, and interpretability. Evaluated through simulations involving demographic bias shocks, concept drift, and unexpected disruptions, AURORA-AI outperformed several established controllers by achieving faster recovery, improving key performance quantiles, reducing demographic parity gaps, and maintaining system stability. The framework's closed-loop policy combines Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman feedback control with Lyapunov-based stability monitoring, enabling it to adapt resource distribution in real time to maximize a composite utility function. Compared to static and reinforcement learning-based controllers, AURORA-AI demonstrated immediate recovery from severe disruptions and enhanced fairness metrics, indicating its potential for practical deployment in human-centric AI applications. These results suggest that incorporating fairness-aware adaptive orchestration grounded in stability theory offers a promising approach to maintaining resilient and equitable AI systems amid changing operational environments and unexpected challenges.

item.title: Researchers propose semantic early-stopping for iterative LLM agent loops to reduce token use by 38% without quality loss, validated on multi-hop question answering tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed a semantic early-stopping method for iterative loops in multi-agent large language models (LLMs), such as a Writer and Critic system, to reduce token usage without sacrificing answer quality. Unlike traditional fixed iteration caps that stop processing after a set number of steps regardless of progress, this approach halts the loop when consecutive draft embeddings show minimal semantic change and the answer quality plateaus. This method was validated on multi-hop retrieval-augmented question answering tasks, achieving a 38% reduction in token use while maintaining comparable answer quality. The study provides a theoretical foundation proving deterministic termination and well-definedness of the stopping criterion, supported by machine-checked claims. It also introduces an efficient evaluation protocol that replays stopping policies over identical draft trajectories and caches judge calls to enable low-cost, paired comparisons of efficiency versus quality. Empirical results on the HotpotQA dataset demonstrate that a judge-free semantic stopper effectively reduces operational tokens, whereas a quality-gated variant that judges each round incurs higher costs. The findings suggest that the challenge lies more in selecting the best iteration rather than deciding when to stop.

item.title: arXiv paper reviews external validity indexes for clustering evaluation with ground truth, recommending centroid index for cluster-level and pair-set index for point-level measures [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new paper on arXiv reviews common external validity indexes used for evaluating clustering results when ground truth data is available. The authors recommend the centroid index (CI) as an intuitive measure at the cluster level due to its explainable outcomes. For more detailed, point-level evaluation, they suggest the pair-set index (PSI), which offers a normalized score unbiased by cluster sizes, while clustering accuracy (ACC) or other set-matching measures are suitable when all points should be weighted equally.

item.title: Researchers present JERP, a method for joint learning of experiential rules and policies in large language model agents, improving decision performance in complex interactive tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed JERP, a method that jointly learns experiential rules and policies for large language model (LLM) agents operating in multi-step interactive environments. JERP updates a long-term rule pool and the agent's policy using the same interaction data, allowing the agent to retrieve relevant rules during decision-making and refine both rules and policy after each episode. This approach maintains alignment between the evolving policy and the rule pool, improving decision performance in complex tasks. The method addresses limitations of previous approaches that either stored experience as separate natural-language rules or updated model parameters without effectively correcting local mistakes in sparse-reward settings. Experiments on environments like AlfWorld and WebShop demonstrate that JERP consistently enhances the agent's performance by integrating stable behaviors into the model while adapting to new experiences.

item.title: Researchers introduce OpenRCA 2.0 with PAVE protocol for step-wise causal supervision in root cause analysis, revealing LLMs recover exact root causes in 20.7% of cases across 11 models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced OpenRCA 2.0, a new benchmark for root cause analysis (RCA) that includes step-wise causal annotations using the PAVE protocol. This approach addresses a key limitation in existing datasets by labeling not only the root cause but also the causal propagation path from cause to observed symptom, enabling more rigorous evaluation of large language models (LLMs) in multi-step reasoning and long-context understanding. Testing 11 advanced LLMs on OpenRCA 2.0 revealed that they correctly identify the exact root cause in only 20.7% of cases on average. The study found that while LLMs often identify at least one correct root cause in 76.0% of cases, they struggle to verify the causal path linking the cause to the symptom, succeeding in only 61.5% of cases. This gap highlights a failure mode that outcome-only evaluations miss, underscoring the importance of step-wise causal supervision for developing trustworthy LLM-based RCA agents.

item.title: Researchers propose TOPS, a training-free visual token pruning method for MLLMs that removes up to 77.8% of tokens while preserving or improving performance on LLaVA-NeXT models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced TOPS, a training-free and model-agnostic visual token pruning method designed to improve the efficiency of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by removing up to 77.8% of visual tokens without sacrificing performance. Applied to LLaVA-NeXT models, TOPS maintained or slightly improved performance on both 7B and 13B parameter versions, demonstrating its ability to reduce computational overhead while preserving model accuracy. The approach is based on a first-principles formulation called Token Optimal Preservation Sets, guided by three principles: Task Relevance, Information Coverage, and Semantic Diversity. Extensive testing across seven MLLM architectures and fourteen benchmarks showed that TOPS outperforms existing pruning methods, which often struggle with redundancy or lack alignment with user instructions. By effectively pruning redundant visual tokens, TOPS not only enhances inference efficiency but also has the potential to reduce hallucinations in MLLMs. This advancement could influence future designs of lightweight multimodal models, making them more practical for real-world applications.

item.title: Researchers introduce process harness mechanism to integrate agentic layers with legacy workflows using the Task-Decision-Flow model and CUGA FLO implementation for adaptive business process management [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the process harness, a novel mechanism that integrates agentic layers with existing legacy workflows in business process management without replacing the underlying workflow engines. This approach uses a policy-governed agentic layer that intercepts key control points to provide reasoning, adaptation, and oversight while maintaining the deterministic workflow engine's structural control. The process harness is formalized through the Task-Decision-Flow (TDF) model, which organizes reasoning across three types of agents-TaskAgent, DecisionAgent, and FlowAgent-each operating under explicit policies within the system's overall governance framework. The team implemented this model in CUGA FLO and demonstrated its effectiveness using a loan approval workflow that leverages all three agent types and supports regulatory overrides through hook mechanisms. This design uniquely balances imperative requirements, enforced by deterministic workflow execution, with normative requirements, enabled by policy-driven agent autonomy at designated control points, allowing adaptive and compliant business process management.

item.title: Researchers propose GAversary, a genetic algorithm using GloVe embeddings to generate black-box adversarial attacks that reduce natural language model accuracy from 76.8% to 5.8% on benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced GAversary, a genetic algorithm that uses GloVe embeddings to generate black-box adversarial attacks on natural language models. This method requires only the model's output logits to guide its search and significantly reduces model accuracy on benchmark tests, dropping it from 76.8% to as low as 5.8%. GAversary outperforms existing attacks like BAE and A2T in effectiveness, though it modifies more words and slightly decreases semantic similarity to the original text. GAversary's approach improves upon previous genetic algorithms by leveraging GloVe embeddings for word replacement mutations, enhancing the semantic relevance of adversarial examples. The algorithm was tested on multiple benchmark datasets and well-known models, demonstrating its ability to substantially degrade model performance while operating as a black-box attack. The trade-offs include increased word perturbations and a modest rise in runtime compared to other methods.

item.title: Researchers propose BINEVAL, a binary-question framework for interpretable LLM evaluation and self-improvement, showing strong results on factual consistency benchmarks and enabling prompt optimization [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced BINEVAL, a novel framework designed to improve the evaluation of large language model (LLM) outputs by breaking down assessment criteria into simple binary questions. This approach generates detailed, interpretable feedback and overall scores that are easier to understand and use for prompt refinement. BINEVAL has demonstrated strong performance on benchmarks like SummEval, Topical-Chat, and QAGS, particularly excelling in assessing factual consistency compared to existing methods such as UniEval and G-Eval. The framework operates by using a meta-prompt to create fine-grained evaluation questions, which an LLM answers independently for each output. This method not only aligns well with human judgment distributions but also avoids common issues like ceiling effects, enabling better differentiation between marginal and clearly flawed outputs. Additionally, BINEVAL's question-level feedback supports iterative prompt optimization, enhancing both evaluator and generation prompts across different tasks and models. Overall, BINEVAL offers a task-agnostic, training-free, and interpretable evaluation system that combines robust empirical results with practical diagnostic and optimization benefits, addressing key challenges in LLM output evaluation.

item.title: Researchers introduce EO-WM, a physically informed video diffusion transformer for probabilistic Earth observation forecasting that improves vegetation decline prediction under extreme weather conditions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed EO-WM, a video diffusion transformer designed for probabilistic Earth observation forecasting that improves predictions of vegetation decline under extreme weather conditions. This model treats Earth observation forecasting as a weather-driven world modeling problem, incorporating meteorological forcing through a physically informed conditioning framework that separates climatological baselines, weather anomalies, and cumulative physical stress signals. EO-WM enhances the accuracy of vegetation degradation forecasts by better capturing sustained heat and drought stress compared to existing methods. To assess the model's performance beyond standard reconstruction metrics, the researchers introduced two diagnostic benchmarks: the Extreme Summer Benchmark, which evaluates severity-aware predictions of vegetation decline during extreme weather, and the Seasonal Matched-Pair Benchmark, which tests forecast responsiveness to changed weather conditions. Experiments demonstrated that EO-WM reduces error in predicting vegetation decline amplitude by 5.63% and improves directional hit rate by 7.80%, while maintaining competitive performance on pixel-level metrics. The model and benchmarks will be made publicly available to support further research in Earth observation forecasting.

item.title: Researchers compare simulation-based inference with MCMC for rapid Bayesian calibration of COVID-19 epidemiological models using ICU data from Germany in 2020 [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have evaluated simulation-based inference (SBI) as a faster alternative to Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) for Bayesian calibration of a mechanistic SECIR epidemiological model using COVID-19 ICU occupancy data from Germany in 2020. The study compared SBI and MCMC across multiple epidemic phases, including both short 31-day inference windows and a longer 201-day reconstruction involving multiple transmission changes. SBI produced posterior distributions closely matching those from MCMC while significantly reducing computational time by leveraging GPU resources. The analysis showed that SBI accurately reproduced observed ICU trajectories and maintained the dominant posterior structure even in the more complex 201-day scenario, despite increased uncertainty. While MCMC required about 1000 seconds for the 31-day problems and over 19,000 seconds for the 201-day problem, SBI achieved comparable results in approximately 60-70 seconds and 157 seconds respectively. These findings suggest that SBI offers a rapid and computationally efficient framework for near-real-time Bayesian calibration of epidemiological models, facilitating timely outbreak analysis and public health decision-making.

item.title: Researchers study prompt injection in automated résumé screening with large language models, finding manipulation improves rankings when rare but collapses as it becomes widespread, raising fairness concerns [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have examined the impact of prompt injection-subtle self-promotional text without new qualifications-on automated résumé screening using large language models (LLMs). Their controlled experiments reveal that prompt injection can improve applicant rankings when résumé quality is similar and few candidates use this tactic, but its effectiveness declines sharply as more candidates engage in manipulation, eventually collapsing when widespread. In cases with varied candidate quality, prompt injection is generally less effective but can sometimes allow lower-quality applicants to outrank higher-quality ones, raising concerns about fairness. The study highlights that LLM-based hiring systems are most vulnerable to manipulation when candidate quality differences are small and prompt injection is rare. The researchers have made their code and resources publicly available to support further investigation into this issue.

item.title: Researchers analyze co-failure rates limiting accuracy gains from combining 67 large language models across routing, voting, and mixture-of-agents methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers analyzed the limitations of combining multiple large language models (LLMs) through methods like routing, voting, and mixture-of-agents to improve accuracy. They identified a key constraint, termed beta, which represents the rate at which all models fail on the same query, capping the maximum achievable accuracy. Their study across 67 models from 21 providers revealed that traditional metrics like average pairwise error correlation do not capture this co-failure rate, which significantly impacts the potential gains from multi-model systems. The team applied statistical bounds to estimate beta and found that existing models underestimate the frequency of simultaneous failures, especially in tasks like open-ended mathematics and code execution. They also observed that the format of questions influences co-failure rates, with free-response formats showing higher beta values than multiple-choice. Their findings suggest that improvements in multi-model accuracy primarily come from models failing on different queries rather than simply increasing the number of models combined. These insights highlight the importance of understanding co-failure dynamics when designing ensemble LLM systems and suggest that without strong query-level routing signals, combining models may rarely outperform the best single model on verifiable tasks. This research provides a framework for better evaluating and optimizing multi-model approaches in artificial intelligence.

item.title: Researchers propose language-based digital twins using large language models to mimic elderly conversational behavior for early cognitive impairment detection and continuous health monitoring [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a language-based digital twin framework that uses large language models to replicate the conversational behavior of elderly individuals. This approach aims to aid early detection of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) by analyzing language and conversational patterns as non-invasive biomarkers. The framework incorporates stylometric cues and contextual metadata to create personalized digital twins for continuous cognitive health monitoring. The team introduced a multi-head conditional variational autoencoder to assess the fidelity and cognitive consistency of the digital twins by measuring reconstruction quality and predicting cognitive scores. Experiments on the I-CONECT dataset demonstrated that these digital twins maintain identity-specific characteristics and achieve performance comparable to real data, outperforming baseline GPT-generated responses. This research highlights the potential of language-based digital twins as a scalable, non-invasive tool for personalized healthcare, offering continuous monitoring and early intervention opportunities for cognitive decline in elderly populations.

item.title: Researchers benchmark four open-weight language models on Global AI Dataset v2 to assess geographic bias and accuracy in AI governance across 227 countries from 2010 to 2023 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers evaluated four open-weight large language models (LLMs) using the Global AI Dataset v2, which includes 24,453 verified indicators across 227 countries from 2010 to 2023, to assess geographic bias and accuracy in AI governance analysis. The study addressed limitations of previous research by focusing on open models, using data within the models' training periods, and applying a detailed five-category classification of model responses to distinguish between accurate answers, confident fabrications, and honest uncertainty. The evaluation involved approximately 2,990 country-metric-year observations across six years, covering 18 indicators aligned with the IEEE IRAI 2026 framework. Researchers used mixed-effects logistic regression and difference-in-differences analysis to measure disparities in model accuracy related to geographic representation in training data, highlighting the challenges LLMs face when analyzing underrepresented countries in AI governance contexts.

item.title: Researchers present Know2Guess, a contamination-aware multi-zone benchmark with 1,200 items for evaluating knowledge boundaries and abstention behavior in large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Know2Guess, a contamination-aware, multi-zone benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' ability to distinguish between supported answers and unsupported guesses while accounting for data contamination and refusal behaviors. The benchmark includes 1,200 items across five domains with explicit abstention expectations and contamination-risk metadata, enabling assessment of models' transitions from answering to abstaining under controlled conditions. The study tested models such as FLAN-T5, Qwen2.5-Instruct, and Llama-3-Instruct using various prompt strategies and parsing methods. Results showed that while instruction-tuned models demonstrated some ability to selectively abstain, challenges remain in calibration and handling answer-expected zones. Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct achieved the highest reliability, but no model fully solved the benchmark, highlighting ongoing difficulties in balancing answerability, abstention, refusal, and contamination. The dataset and evaluation protocol are publicly available for further research.

item.title: Researchers find post-training on helpfulness data degrades mid-trained compassion values in Llama 3.1 8B model, with coding-domain post-training better preserving values and reasoning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers examined how different post-training domains affect the retention of compassion values in the Llama 3.1 8B language model, which was mid-trained on compassion-oriented data. They found that post-training focused on helpfulness significantly reduced the model's animal compassion and moral reasoning abilities compared to coding-domain post-training, as measured by the Animal Harm Benchmark and the Moral Reasoning Under Uncertainty benchmark. This degradation was consistent across two training methods and datasets but did not appear in multilingual moral reasoning tests. The study revealed that compassion values instilled during mid-training are more deeply encoded and transfer better across languages than reasoning improvements from domain-specific post-training. Coding-domain post-training preserved these mid-trained values more effectively than helpfulness-focused training, without impairing general reasoning skills. These findings suggest that for models trained with value-laden data, selecting the post-training domain carefully is crucial to maintaining desired ethical attributes.

item.title: Study finds large language models perform well on text-only statics problems but accuracy drops with diagrams and multi-step reasoning challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent study evaluated the problem-solving abilities of large language models (LLMs), specifically ChatGPT, on statics questions commonly found in mechanical engineering education. The research found that while LLMs perform well on text-only statics problems, their accuracy declines when diagrams are included and when problems require multi-step reasoning. This suggests that the models struggle more with complex reasoning and consistently applying visual information than with image recognition itself. The study used a model distillation approach to extract 25 text-only statics questions and created additional datasets by adding diagrams and altering numerical values. The findings highlight the limitations of current LLMs in handling engineering problems that combine visual and textual information, emphasizing the need for improved multi-step reasoning capabilities in these models.

item.title: Researchers find assertive and explicit linguistic features in fine-tuning data increase Llama-3.2-1B's pro-animal-welfare reasoning, while hedged and sensory descriptions dilute it [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers analyzed how different linguistic features in fine-tuning data influence Llama-3.2-1B's reasoning about animal welfare. They found that assertive and explicit language, including moral vocabulary, emotion words, and narrative elements, significantly enhance the model's pro-animal-welfare stance, while hedged language and concrete sensory descriptions tend to weaken it. The study suggests that clearly asserting a position in animal-welfare texts is more effective for training language models than neutral scene descriptions. The research used vocabulary-matched stance-contrast probes on a dedicated animal-welfare benchmark to measure the impact of ten linguistic features. Seven features strengthened pro-animal-welfare reasoning, one had no significant effect, and two diluted the stance. This insight offers practical guidance for authors whose work may be included in training corpora for large language models, emphasizing the importance of explicit advocacy over neutral narration.

item.title: Researchers introduce ContextForge for efficient context recycling in long-horizon LLM inference, improving consistency and reducing token use in 15-turn healthcare query benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ContextForge, a system designed to improve the performance of large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon conversational tasks by efficiently recycling context. ContextForge combines structured query generation, external memory retrieval, and controlled synthesis to maintain relevant information across multiple turns without replaying the entire context, reducing token usage while preserving answer quality. The system was tested on a 15-turn healthcare query benchmark, demonstrating improved consistency and reduced token consumption compared to baseline models, with comparable accuracy. This approach addresses the limitations of LLMs in handling extended conversations due to context window constraints and inefficient token use. By enabling the reuse of prior computations, ContextForge offers a practical solution for extending LLM capabilities in complex, multi-turn reasoning tasks without the need for larger context windows or retraining. The researchers have made their code and evaluation materials publicly available for further exploration.

item.title: Researchers use Nonviolent Communication constraints to reduce conversational escalation in large language model dialogues, improving interaction stability with resistant users [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a method to reduce conversational escalation in large language model (LLM) dialogues by applying constraints based on Nonviolent Communication (NVC) principles. These constraints guide LLMs to avoid blame, focus on users' emotional experiences, and seek clarification before offering advice, aiming to de-escalate conflicts in emotionally charged interactions. Using a dual-agent simulation framework across various instruction-tuned models and levels of user resistance, the study demonstrates that NVC-constrained prompting consistently lowers escalation and stabilizes conversations with resistant users. This approach suggests that simple, process-oriented communication guidelines can enhance the trustworthiness and safety of LLM interactions in conflict-prone settings.

item.title: Researchers present NEST-V1, a lightweight multimodal system translating Nepali spoken words into emotion-conditioned sign language avatars with 81.1% ASR and 79.21% emotion recognition accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed NEST-V1, a lightweight multimodal system that translates Nepali spoken words into emotion-conditioned sign language avatars. The system uses a shared acoustic encoder for simultaneous automatic speech recognition and emotion classification, achieving 81.1% accuracy in speech recognition and 79.21% in emotion recognition on a dataset of 600 audio samples. This pilot study focuses on four common Nepali words expressed in three emotional states to validate the approach. NEST-V1 demonstrates 37% greater parameter efficiency compared to separate models while maintaining a compact size suitable for edge deployment. The framework establishes a foundation for emotion-aware sign language translation in low-resource languages and offers scalability for expanding vocabulary and emotional expressions. These preliminary results suggest the potential for real-time, emotionally expressive sign language communication systems to benefit the hearing-impaired community, with opportunities for further development.

item.title: Paper analyzes legal and technical aspects of generative AI music systems under US copyright law, highlighting risks of lyric copying and gaps in vocal likeness protection [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A recent paper analyzes the legal and technical challenges of generative AI music systems under U.S. copyright law, focusing on issues such as unauthorized lyric copying and the use of AI-generated vocals that imitate real artists. It examines whether creating and monetizing songs using protected lyrics combined with synthetic voices violates exclusive rights under Title 17 of the U.S. Code, highlighting the distinction between protections for musical compositions and sound recordings. The study reviews relevant copyright doctrines, state-level voice-cloning laws, and recent legal cases to map AI technical components to associated legal risks. It finds that while unauthorized lyric use poses a significant infringement risk, AI-generated vocal likenesses typically fall outside federal sound recording protections and instead raise state publicity rights concerns. The paper identifies a regulatory gap in federal law regarding synthesized vocal likeness and offers policy recommendations for clearer rules governing AI music creation.

item.title: Researchers present a structured-data pipeline converting Hindi WordNet into 1.25 million instruction-response pairs to fine-tune a 12B-parameter model for specialized conversational AI in low-resource languages [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a structured-data pipeline that transforms Hindi WordNet into 1.25 million instruction-response pairs to fine-tune a 12-billion-parameter language model. This approach uses resource-efficient techniques like LoRA with 4-bit quantization to create a specialized conversational AI system tailored for low-resource languages. Evaluations with a Hindi language learning chatbot show that this system outperforms general-purpose models in pedagogical effectiveness while maintaining strong semantic performance and consistency. The methodology demonstrates how expert-curated lexical databases can serve as a foundation for developing specialized AI without relying on large training corpora. This proof-of-concept using Hindi suggests the approach can be applied to any language with existing WordNet resources, addressing a significant gap in AI accessibility for many low-resource languages and offering a practical alternative to data-intensive methods.

item.title: arXiv paper analyzes generative AI's impact on creative industries, highlighting OpenAI's Sora model release, UK copyright tensions, and new AI-driven roles in production pipelines [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A recent arXiv paper analyzes the transformative impact of generative artificial intelligence on creative industries, highlighting the December 2024 release of OpenAI's Sora video model as a pivotal moment. The study introduces the Human-AI Agency Continuum to map collaboration between humans and AI in creative work and identifies a "slop ceiling," where AI-generated content, despite making up 44% of uploads, accounts for only 1-3% of audience streams. It also examines the UK government's 2025 consultation on AI and copyright, revealing significant tensions between technology companies and creative professionals. The paper explores how major studios like Disney and Netflix are adapting to AI-augmented production pipelines, including the emergence of new roles such as prompt engineers and AI orchestrators. It discusses challenges like coordination breakdowns in creative supply chains and proposes principles for managing the transition, emphasizing transparency, consent, compensation, and human-centered design. Supplementary materials provide detailed quantitative analysis, a glossary, and insights into AI adoption and related social dynamics.

item.title: Researchers propose a multi-layer AI framework for analyzing information landscapes across source reliability, bias, framing, and propagation to support nuanced media analysis and information disorder research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a multi-layer AI framework designed to analyze information landscapes in the context of information disorder. Unlike traditional binary fact-checking approaches, this framework evaluates political and media content across various dimensions such as source reliability, factual structure, framing, bias, emotional activation, manipulation patterns, and propagation dynamics. The aim is to create a structured representation of the informational environment surrounding events, entities, or narratives to support more nuanced media analysis. The framework emphasizes epistemic mapping, providing a transparent, multi-dimensional view of how facts, interpretations, actors, and narratives interact over time. The paper outlines the conceptual architecture, analytical layers, and methodological rationale behind this approach, aiming to enhance the development of explainable and critically useful AI tools for researching information disorder.

item.title: Study finds ChatGPT and Claude disagree on two-thirds of brand recommendations but converge on diagnosing failure modes 95% of the time across 7,763 joint failures [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study analyzing product recommendations from ChatGPT and Claude reveals that the two AI providers disagree on brand recommendations about two-thirds of the time. However, when both fail to recommend a brand, they concur on the failure mode-discoverability, compellingness, or positioning-95% of the time across 7,763 joint failures. This high agreement increases as brand prominence decreases, reaching nearly complete consensus for less well-known regional brands. The research highlights that ChatGPT and Claude use different generative approaches to select brands, with Anthropic relying more on prior knowledge than OpenAI. Despite these differences, their convergence on diagnosing failure modes is particularly significant for improving recommendations for long-tail brands. Addressing these failure modes enhances brand visibility on both platforms, though strategies for category leaders require more provider-specific adjustments.

item.title: Researchers introduce Governance Inversion Hypothesis explaining how increased AI regulation may reduce organisational operational control through authority fragmentation and procedural complexity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed the Governance Inversion Hypothesis (GIH) to address a paradox in AI governance: as regulatory measures and technological complexity increase, organizations may become more formally governed yet lose operational control over AI systems. Contrary to the common belief that stronger regulation enhances accountability and oversight, the study argues that increased governance formalization can fragment authority and complicate procedures, ultimately weakening an organization's ability to manage AI effectively. The paper outlines four mechanisms-authority fragmentation, symbolic governance expansion, externalization of control, and authority paralysis-that contribute to this decline in operational control. It suggests that layered and complex governance structures can reduce technical visibility and intervention capacity over AI infrastructures. By extending institutional decoupling theory, the authors highlight that expanding governance may paradoxically undermine operational coherence rather than strengthen it. This research implies that the main risk in AI governance is not the lack of regulatory frameworks but the emergence of institutions that appear well-governed while progressively losing their capacity to govern effectively. This insight calls for a reevaluation of how AI regulations are designed and implemented to ensure they support, rather than hinder, organizational control.

item.title: Researchers develop open-source economic index measuring AI adoption and capability across occupations using user-LLM chat data and O*NET tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an open-source economic index to measure AI adoption and capability across various occupations by analyzing publicly available user-LLM chat data and O*NET task information. Their findings indicate that sectors such as finance, computer science, and the arts exhibit the highest rates of AI adoption. To assess AI capabilities, the team created benchmark scenarios based on O*NET occupations and tasks, testing the Kimi-k2.5 model with an OpenAI agents SDK across nine frequently represented occupations in their index. The evaluation revealed that while AI systems can successfully execute high-level workflows, they often struggle with detailed aspects, such as specific tool usage. This work provides a replicable framework for tracking AI integration in the workforce and assessing its practical performance on discrete labor tasks.

item.title: Researchers present Dot-Flik, a scalable edge AI architecture for distributed insect monitoring with motion-informed frame filtering and hierarchical IoT design, validated on low-cost hardware with real-time performance and energy savings [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Dot-Flik, a scalable edge AI system designed for distributed insect monitoring that addresses the challenges of high hardware costs, energy consumption, and dependence on centralized processing. The system features a motion-informed frame filtering algorithm that reduces irrelevant data at the edge without requiring deep learning on the sensing device, and a hierarchical IoT architecture that separates data acquisition from AI classification to enhance scalability and coverage. The approach was validated through outdoor deployments using low-cost hardware, demonstrating significant frame reduction, real-time 30 FPS performance with computational headroom, energy savings up to 22.6%, and support for multiple concurrent edge streams per central node. These results suggest Dot-Flik offers a practical, efficient foundation for dense, low-cost biodiversity monitoring networks, particularly suited for urban environments.

item.title: Researchers propose privacy-aware multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for dynamic VR slice management in 6G SD-RAN, improving throughput by 34% and reducing privacy leakage by 85% in simulations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a privacy-aware multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework to manage dynamic virtual reality (VR) slices in 6G Software-Defined Radio Access Networks (SD-RANs). This approach aims to meet the ultra-low latency and high throughput demands of VR services by enabling cooperative agents to optimize resource allocation across end-to-end VR links while safeguarding user data privacy. The framework integrates mobility prediction and an information bottleneck encoder to enhance secure collaboration among agents. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements over traditional methods, including a 34% increase in throughput, a 28% reduction in resource usage, and an 85% decrease in privacy leakage, supporting reliable immersive VR experiences in future 6G networks.

item.title: Researchers propose Geo-FairFed, a geometric fairness-aware routing system using hyperbolic graph neural networks and federated optimization to improve latency, energy use, and fairness in 6G and IoT edge networks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Geo-FairFed, a routing system designed for emerging 6G and edge-intelligent networks that integrates hyperbolic graph neural networks with federated optimization to enhance latency, energy efficiency, and fairness across distributed edge nodes. The system models network topologies on a negatively curved manifold to capture hierarchical and asymmetric connections, while a global aggregator enforces fairness by minimizing routing loss and inequality based on Jain's fairness index. This approach aims to balance performance equitably among nodes rather than focusing solely on aggregate metrics. Theoretical analysis confirms convergence under certain curvature conditions and demonstrates that the fairness component leads to a Pareto-improving equilibrium in routing performance. Simulations on dynamic 6G-edge and IoT network topologies show that Geo-FairFed reduces average latency by 20%, cuts energy consumption by 17%, and improves fairness by up to 21% compared to existing federated and geometric routing protocols. These results suggest that embedding network topology in hyperbolic space and incorporating fairness into federated learning can significantly improve the efficiency and equity of large-scale network routing.

item.title: Study finds GPT-5.1, Gemini 3 Pro, and DeepSeek-V3.2 suggest narrower research methods than recent arXiv computer science papers, with significant provider bias and reduced methodological diversity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent study analyzed how Large Language Models (LLMs) like GPT-5.1, Gemini 3 Pro, and DeepSeek-V3.2 suggest research methodologies when prompted with questions extracted from 1,000 recent computer science papers on arXiv. The study found that these LLMs tend to recommend a much narrower range of methods compared to the diverse approaches documented in the papers, with a significant bias toward certain model providers. This narrowing effect was consistent across models and was most pronounced in the choice of model providers, indicating a concentration in default methodological suggestions. The researchers mapped methods from both LLM outputs and paper inventories into a shared taxonomy and measured divergences across dimensions such as dataset task type and evaluation metrics. They observed that single-occurrence academic models were underrepresented in LLM suggestions, while reused academic or community models were slightly overrepresented. The study also confirmed that LLM outputs are query-specific but filtered through a limited set of options, which may lead researchers relying solely on these suggestions to inadvertently restrict their methodological search space.

item.title: arXiv:2606.26139 presents a multiscale model coupling strategic exit-join decisions with tactical consensus dynamics to analyze coalition formation and stability in multi-agent systems
item.description: The paper presents a multiscale model that integrates strategic exit-and-join decisions with tactical consensus dynamics to study coalition formation and stability in multi-agent systems. It models coalition value as emerging from within-group information aggregation and uses Aumann-Dreze payoffs, switching frictions, and acceptance rules to govern coalition reconfiguration. The framework features a fast-slow dynamic where coalition value arises from consensus processes, while coalition structures evolve through incentive-driven membership changes. The analysis identifies conditions for various equilibrium states, including unanimity, segregation, and polarization, and establishes fixed-point characterizations for the coupled dynamics. Numerical experiments reveal an instability-consensus paradox, where low switching barriers can hinder strategic convergence but promote sufficient mixing to achieve global tactical consensus. This work offers a unified approach to understanding coalition formation, consensus mechanisms, information aggregation, and strategic stability in multi-agent environments.

item.title: Researchers introduce unsupervised Video Memory Transformers for real-time obstacle detection on autonomous agricultural rover, achieving state-of-the-art results on rapeseed dataset [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Video Memory Transformers for Anomaly Detection (VMTAD), an unsupervised method designed to detect obstacles in real-time for autonomous agricultural rovers. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional sensors like LiDAR, which cannot detect obstacles beneath plant canopies, and supervised camera-based methods that struggle with unseen obstacles. VMTAD uses a transformer architecture with a memory module that processes temporal context from previous frames, enabling effective detection in dynamic environments without requiring labeled data. The system was tested on the 'Grillion' agricultural rover using a challenging rapeseed dataset, achieving state-of-the-art results with detection and segmentation AUC scores of 0.973 and 0.997, respectively. A lightweight version of the model balances high accuracy with real-time inference speeds of 14 milliseconds, which is crucial for ensuring operational safety by allowing timely stopping responses.

item.title: Researchers propose ARReST method to reduce redundancy in whole-slide image patching, achieving 3% to 60% storage savings while maintaining retrieval accuracy on TCGA pathology data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced ARReST (Antithetical Redundancy Reduction Strategy), a novel method designed to reduce redundancy in whole-slide image (WSI) patching for digital pathology. ARReST targets patches that contribute little to distinguishing between different tissue classes, pruning them to significantly decrease the number of patches indexed without compromising retrieval accuracy. This approach achieves storage savings ranging from 3% to 60% while maintaining effective similarity search performance on The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) pathology data. By focusing on cross-class redundancy rather than just within-class duplicates, ARReST preserves morphological diversity and retrieval fidelity, enabling more efficient and scalable indexing of large pathology image repositories. The method reduces storage requirements and computational overhead, facilitating faster similarity searches and supporting the demands of retrieval-augmented generation workflows in clinical AI systems. Extensive experiments across 21 organs in the TCGA dataset demonstrate ARReST's ability to compress indexes substantially while sustaining competitive retrieval results, making it a promising solution for cost-effective and scalable digital pathology infrastructure.

item.title: arXiv paper reviews neural architecture search methods for generative adversarial networks, comparing search strategies and evaluation metrics, and highlighting performance improvements and research gaps [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent paper on arXiv reviews Neural Architecture Search (NAS) methods applied to Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), providing a detailed comparison of different search strategies, evaluation metrics, and performance results. The study highlights how NAS can enhance GAN performance, stability, and efficiency, while also identifying current limitations and areas needing further research. Key insights include the effectiveness of evolutionary and gradient-based algorithms in specific scenarios, the need for evaluation metrics beyond traditional scores like Inception Score and Fréchet Inception Distance, and the importance of diverse datasets for comprehensive assessment. The paper categorizes existing NAS approaches for GANs and discusses their relative strengths, aiming to guide future research in developing more robust and effective NAS techniques. By offering a structured analysis, it contributes to advancing the design and optimization of GAN architectures through automated search methods.

item.title: Researchers propose LCG framework with Sparse Relational Attention for consistent long-context multi-image generation, introducing a new dataset with 600K sequences for training and evaluation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Long-Context Generation (LCG), a new framework designed to enhance consistency in multi-image text-to-image generation over extended sequences, addressing challenges in applications like comics and storyboards. LCG uses Sparse Relational Attention (SRA) to efficiently manage semantic and layout information across long visual contexts, and incorporates a Routing Consistency Constraint (RCC) to maintain structural alignment and reduce appearance drift, even in complex scenes with multiple characters. To facilitate training and evaluation, the team developed the Long-Context Consistency Dataset (LCCD), a large-scale synthetic dataset containing 600,000 training sequences and 1,000 test sequences, each comprising 6 to 20 images focused on character-centric scenarios. Experimental results show that LCG outperforms existing methods in maintaining prompt alignment and character consistency throughout long image sequences, demonstrating its effectiveness for consistent multi-image generation.

item.title: Researchers present KG-TRACE, a neuro-symbolic framework integrating WHO mutation knowledge graph for antimicrobial resistance prediction with 92.5% symbolic coverage and 0.976 AUROC on M. tuberculosis data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed KG-TRACE, a neuro-symbolic framework that integrates the WHO mutation knowledge graph with neural genomic models to improve antimicrobial resistance (AMR) prediction. Tested on Mycobacterium tuberculosis data, KG-TRACE achieved a 0.976 AUROC for isoniazid resistance prediction and provided 92.5% symbolic coverage, grounding neural attributions in established biological pathways rather than relying solely on statistical patterns. The framework combines genomic features with knowledge graph embeddings through an epistemic trust gate that balances neural evidence against symbolic biological knowledge. It introduces the Biological Grounding Ratio (BGR) metric to quantify alignment between model predictions and biological understanding, and it flags uncertain cases for laboratory follow-up, enhancing clinical trust by offering a verifiable audit trail that bridges predictive accuracy with mechanistic interpretability.

item.title: Researchers propose LiMoDE, a two-stage lifelong learning scheme using a mixture of dynamic experts for robot manipulation, demonstrating improved adaptation and performance in simulated and real-world tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced LiMoDE, a novel two-stage lifelong learning framework for robot manipulation that uses a mixture of dynamic experts to enhance continuous task adaptation. The approach involves a multi-task pre-training stage where a dynamic mixture of experts learns prior knowledge by activating different experts based on motion information, followed by a task adaptation stage that combines lifelong and frozen experts to facilitate knowledge transfer for new tasks. LiMoDE has demonstrated improved performance and adaptability in both simulated lifelong learning benchmarks and real-world robotic tasks. This method addresses limitations of previous approaches that struggled with catastrophic forgetting and ineffective skill reuse by proposing an architectural solution rather than relying solely on parameter-efficient fine-tuning or prompt learning. The system introduces a moderate increase in trainable parameters and inference overhead while achieving superior lifelong adaptation, highlighting its potential for developing more generalist and adaptable robotic systems.

item.title: arXiv: Survey presents a five-stage taxonomy of vision-language perception evolution in multimodal large language models, highlighting unified capabilities and future research directions toward general AI [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new survey published on arXiv presents a comprehensive five-stage taxonomy detailing the evolution of vision-language perception in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). The study emphasizes the integration of vision and language as a unified modality, highlighting key models like OpenAI's O-series and DeepSeek's R-series that have advanced perception-centric intelligence. This work aims to provide a foundational framework for understanding MLLM perception and outlines significant milestones and methods across each stage of development. The survey addresses a gap in existing literature by treating vision and language perception as inseparable, contrasting with prior reviews that often consider these modalities separately. It formalizes MLLM perception as an intrinsic capability akin to human innate perception and identifies open challenges and promising research directions. The authors hope this roadmap will guide future innovations toward achieving truly general, unified multimodal intelligence and progress toward artificial general intelligence (AGI).

item.title: arXiv paper presents statistical and structural methods to address limitations in algorithmic fairness paradigms amid socio-technical inequalities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new paper on arXiv explores the limitations of current algorithmic fairness approaches in machine learning, highlighting how these systems reflect and perpetuate existing social inequalities. The research critiques the reliance on deterministic point estimates for fairness auditing and the tendency to treat individuals as isolated cases without considering broader structural contexts. The study emphasizes that early fairness mitigation strategies oversimplified complex socio-technical environments, reducing their effectiveness. By addressing these fundamental issues, the paper aims to improve fairness frameworks to better account for the embedded prejudices and structural inequalities influencing algorithmic decision-making.

item.title: Researchers present CyberChainBench benchmark evaluating AI agents on smart contract security using 541 real-world exploits across 9 EVM chains, with top agent detecting 37.5% vulnerabilities and generating $57.4M exploit profit [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CyberChainBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents' performance in securing smart contracts against real-world vulnerabilities. The benchmark encompasses three tasks-vulnerability detection, exploit generation, and patch synthesis-using data from 541 actual exploit incidents across nine Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) chains. Agents interact with historical blockchain states in controlled environments, with exploits assessed based on economic impact and patches validated through replaying attacks and transactions. The study categorizes vulnerabilities into five types and tests various AI model configurations. Results show a performance gradient, with the top agent achieving 37.5% accuracy in detection, 43.7% in exploitation, and 23.4% in patching. Notably, the leading AI agent, combining Codex with GPT-5.5, generated $57.4 million in exploit profit over 200 cases, at an average cost of $2.39 per case, highlighting both the potential and challenges of AI in smart contract security.

item.title: Researchers release Lacuna, a machine learning research map using LLMs to generate summaries and proposals, outperforming OpenScholar on LitSearch retrieval tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Lacuna, a research map for machine learning that leverages large language models (LLMs) to generate markdown summaries, concept elements, research directions, and proposals from academic papers and metadata. Lacuna maintains links to original sources and is accessible via web, markdown, and MCP interfaces. It outperforms the OpenScholar system on several retrieval tasks, notably achieving higher recall on LitSearch. The team also evaluated Lacuna Deep Research, a multi-stage report agent built on the map, across 25 survey tasks. It demonstrated improved citation precision and report quality compared to GPT-Researcher, indicating its effectiveness in synthesizing and referencing scholarly information for machine learning research.

item.title: Researchers develop multi-task spatiotemporal deep neural network to predict penetration depth and weld seam morphology in laser welding with over 99% accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a multi-task spatiotemporal deep neural network that accurately predicts penetration depth, penetration state, and weld seam morphology in laser penetration welding. Using weld pool images captured by a complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor camera and welding parameters, the model combines convolutional neural networks with state space models to efficiently extract and process spatial-temporal information. The system achieved a prediction accuracy of 99.35% for penetration state, a penetration depth error of 1.79 millimeters, and 95.65% accuracy in reconstructing weld cross-sections. The study also introduces a robust dataset construction method to improve the model's generalization and reliability. This approach offers new methodologies for in-situ quality control in laser welding, potentially enhancing weld quality assessment and monitoring during the manufacturing process.

item.title: Researchers propose a dual-purpose framework using self-supervised Transformers and LLM-distilled taxonomies to improve cross-platform session embeddings for financial services recommendations, boosting recall and reducing log loss [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a dual-purpose framework that leverages self-supervised Transformers and large language model (LLM)-distilled taxonomies to enhance cross-platform session embeddings for financial services recommendations. This approach addresses the challenge of integrating pre-login web interactions with authenticated in-app experiences, which differ significantly in user intent and are difficult to link due to cross-channel entity resolution issues. The framework produces compact session embeddings and interpretable intent labels from raw web clickstreams, improving both quantitative recommendation accuracy and qualitative understanding. The system demonstrated notable improvements in production tasks: it increased macro Recall@1 by 1.88% and reduced Log Loss by 13.38% in mobile homepage tile ranking, while outperforming LLM labels by 4.3% on micro F1 in user conversion prediction. Additionally, the taxonomy distillation layer delivers interpretable labels with minimal latency and only a slight performance trade-off, showing promise for scalable personalization in financial services.

item.title: Researchers present TEMPO-Diffusion, a targeted backdoor attack framework that temporally poisons diffusion models to induce class-specific synthetic data manipulation and high downstream classifier attack success rates [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced TEMPO-Diffusion, a novel targeted backdoor attack framework that temporally poisons diffusion models to manipulate synthetic data generation for specific classes. Unlike traditional noise-based backdoor attacks that rely on input-time triggers and untargeted activation, TEMPO-Diffusion localizes the malicious influence to a temporal, in-distribution exposure, enabling precise attacks on multiple sub-image features and in-painting with time-conditioned triggers. The framework was tested on datasets including CIFAR10, GTSRB, and a newly introduced region-aware traffic-sign dataset called CALISA, demonstrating its ability to reliably poison class-specific synthetic data and achieve high attack success rates in downstream classifiers trained on this data. The study addresses practical security concerns related to the use of backdoored diffusion models for synthetic training data by providing a more stealthy and targeted attack method. TEMPO-Diffusion's capabilities include reconstructing specific features within multiple output images at various locations, enhancing the attack's precision and potential impact on machine learning systems that rely on synthetic data.

item.title: Researchers introduce Hankel Reduced-order Model adapters for long-context fine-tuning, showing improved performance over LoRA on Mistral-7B across multiple benchmarks and tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new fine-tuning method called the Hankel Reduced-order Model (HRM) adapter, which improves performance on long-context tasks compared to existing approaches like LoRA. The HRM adapter, based on state space models and initialized through Balanced Truncation of empirical Hankel Grammians, enables efficient computation using FFT-based parallel scans. Evaluations on the Mistral-7B model show that HRM outperforms LoRA on benchmarks such as LongBench, QuALITY, and QMSum, demonstrating significant gains in accuracy and ROUGE-1 scores. The study also highlights that HRM adapters effectively modulate recurrence in sequence modeling tasks, providing a robust alternative to low-rank adaptation methods. This approach shows consistent superiority across various synthetic state-tracking and character-level language modeling configurations, suggesting its suitability for tasks requiring sequential state accumulation and long-context fine-tuning.

item.title: Researchers introduce the Red Queen Gödel Machine, an evolutionary framework for recursive self-improvement with co-evolving evaluators that improves coding, paper reviewing, and proof grading performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Red Queen Gödel Machine (RQGM), an evolutionary framework designed for recursive self-improvement with co-evolving evaluators that adapt alongside the agents they assess. Unlike traditional methods that rely on fixed evaluation criteria, the RQGM incorporates dynamic, evolving objectives, allowing agents to improve under changing conditions. This approach has demonstrated enhanced performance in coding tasks, scientific paper writing and reviewing, and Olympiad-level proof grading, surpassing previous state-of-the-art results. The RQGM operates by organizing search into epochs with fixed evaluation criteria within each epoch, while allowing the utility function to evolve between epochs. This controlled utility evolution enables reliable self-improvement guarantees despite shifting objectives. Experiments showed that the RQGM improved test pass rates on coding tasks using a complementary agent-as-a-judge code-review signal, which is more efficient in token usage. In scientific domains, co-evolved writers achieved significantly higher acceptance rates, and co-evolved graders improved accuracy. Additionally, the framework addressed biases in paper reviewing by introducing adversarial objectives that ensure reviewers apply consistent standards to both AI-generated and human work.

item.title: Researchers propose Parametric Generalized Adaptive Moment Features for bearing fault diagnosis, demonstrating improved classification and generalization on benchmark gearbox datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a parametric adaptive feature extraction method called Parametric Generalized Adaptive Moment Features (PG-AMF) to improve fault diagnosis in rolling element bearings used in rotating machinery. This approach learns feature characteristics directly from vibration data, capturing multiple complementary signal representations and modeling interactions across sensor channels. Evaluated on a benchmark gearbox bearing dataset with various health conditions, PG-AMF demonstrated superior classification accuracy and generalization compared to traditional methods. The method extracts absolute features related to signal energy, signed moment features reflecting waveform asymmetry, and AC-coupled moment features highlighting dynamic fluctuations. Its structured fusion mechanism enhances fault representation by integrating data from multiple sensors. The improved feature separability was evident through clearer clustering in low-dimensional projections, indicating the approach's effectiveness in capturing diverse signal characteristics. This advancement supports more reliable and interpretable fault diagnosis, which is crucial for industrial safety and predictive maintenance. The proposed framework offers practical applicability for machine health monitoring systems, potentially enabling earlier detection of bearing faults and reducing downtime in industrial operations.

item.title: Researchers introduce EVOM, an LLM-powered agentic meta-evolution framework that automates actor-critic architecture design for reinforcement learning, outperforming baselines on Ant-v4 and HalfCheetah-v4 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed EVOM, an agentic meta-evolution framework that automates the design of actor-critic architectures in reinforcement learning. EVOM uses a bi-level optimization approach where an inner loop trains network weights using proximal policy optimization, while an outer loop, powered by a large language model (LLM) acting as a design agent, iteratively refines architecture programs. This method is fully decoupled from policy execution and environment control. In experiments on the Ant-v4 and HalfCheetah-v4 benchmarks, EVOM outperformed manually designed architectures, LLM-guided random search, and the state-of-the-art LLM-guided programmatic policy search method MLES. Ablation studies confirmed that both the meta-evolution process and the LLM design agent are essential for achieving superior performance, highlighting EVOM's potential to advance automated architecture design in reinforcement learning.

item.title: Researchers propose hybrid semantic search combining SVD-truncated document embeddings and CKKS-encrypted query reranking to enhance privacy under a restricted threat model [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a hybrid approach to enhance privacy in semantic search by combining truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) of document embeddings with homomorphic encryption of query reranking using the CKKS scheme. This method protects the static document collection through geometric transformations while securing dynamic queries cryptographically, aiming to balance privacy and performance at scale. The approach maintains ranking quality on large datasets with sub-second latency and significantly reduces the risk of reconstructing original documents from leaked vectors under a defined threat model. The study demonstrates that while the encrypted query reranking ensures cryptographic confidentiality, the document protection relies on empirical obfuscation via SVD truncation and secret rotations rather than cryptographic primitives. The researchers also evaluate the system against stronger adversaries, noting limitations such as potential recovery of transformations with sufficient leaked data. Overall, this hybrid scheme offers a practical middle ground between fully homomorphic encryption, which is computationally intensive, and noise-based privacy methods that degrade search accuracy.

item.title: Researchers use small language models to augment systematic review of social-physical human-robot interaction, identifying 10% more relevant papers missed by human reviewers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have explored the use of small language models (SLMs) with fewer than 1.5 billion parameters to assist in the systematic review of social-physical human-robot interaction (spHRI) literature. Although these models did not match the accuracy of human reviewers, they operated much faster and identified 10.29% more relevant papers that human reviewers had missed, demonstrating their potential to augment expert efforts in large-scale literature reviews. The study highlights challenges in spHRI research due to fragmented terminology and inconsistent methodologies, which complicate comprehensive synthesis. By employing an ensemble of SLMs for title and abstract screening, the researchers improved the scalability and sustainability of the review process without replacing human expertise. These findings suggest that integrating SLMs into systematic review workflows can enhance the thoroughness and efficiency of literature surveys in rapidly evolving interdisciplinary fields like spHRI, potentially accelerating research progress and knowledge consolidation.

item.title: Researchers introduce SOLAR, an AI-powered framework that automatically derives validated Speed-of-Light performance bounds from PyTorch and JAX code for deep learning model optimization [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SOLAR, an AI-powered framework that automatically derives validated Speed-of-Light (SOL) performance bounds from PyTorch and JAX code to optimize deep learning models. SOLAR addresses the challenge of manually computing theoretical minimum execution times on target hardware by translating source programs into an intermediate representation and analytically calculating SOL bounds, providing comprehensive operator coverage and validated results without observed violations. The framework combines a large language model frontend with deterministic processes to convert code into an executable form, then into an einsum graph, and finally computes unfused, fused, and cache-aware SOL bounds. Evaluations on various benchmarks and workloads demonstrate SOLAR's capabilities in headroom analysis, identifying optimization opportunities, cross-platform exploration, and hardware provisioning based on inverse-roofline models.

item.title: Researchers propose diffusion-based generative model for global sea state estimation using five-day wind history, achieving faster probabilistic wave forecasting and calibrated ensemble predictions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a diffusion-based generative model for global sea state estimation that uses five days of wind history to produce faster and probabilistic wave forecasts. This model directly samples the complex conditional distribution of sea state variables without relying on autoregressive time-stepping, enabling efficient and calibrated ensemble predictions beyond traditional bulk variables like significant wave height. Trained on a 30-year global hindcast dataset, the model significantly accelerates computation compared to conventional spectral wave models while maintaining skillful predictions. It also estimates additional sea state characteristics such as Stokes drift and mean square slope, offering a comprehensive approach to sea state modeling. The new method presents a promising avenue for integrating probabilistic wave forecasting into operational maritime applications and coupled earth system models, potentially improving the efficiency and accuracy of climate simulations and ensemble-based predictions.

item.title: arXiv:2606.26397 introduces a preference-conditioned Bellman operator for deterministic Pareto-optimal policy synthesis in multi-objective reinforcement learning with proven convergence and policy extraction methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
