item.description: The paper introduces a new preference-conditioned Bellman operator for Multi-Objective Markov Decision Processes (MOMDPs) that enables the computation of deterministic Pareto-optimal policies. This operator, inspired by Chebyshev scalarization, is proven to upper-bound the true Pareto frontier and converges monotonically to a coverage set of this frontier, allowing for the extraction of deterministic policies aligned with any given preference. The approach addresses the limitations of traditional reinforcement learning methods that aggregate multiple objectives into a single scalar reward, which often fails to capture the full range of optimal trade-offs. The authors demonstrate that their method can recover complex trade-offs and synthesize policies that remain approximately Pareto-optimal, ensuring comprehensive coverage of the Pareto frontier. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the algorithm in producing deterministic policies that reflect diverse preference conditions, offering a robust solution for multi-objective reinforcement learning challenges.

item.title: Researchers propose a safe AGI architecture based on closed reentry neural loops enabling self-modeling and intrinsic goal preservation with machine-verified proofs and deployable implementations [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed a novel architecture for safe artificial general intelligence (AGI) based on closed reentry neural loops, which enable self-modeling and intrinsic goal preservation. Unlike traditional feedforward networks, this design incorporates structural cycles that mathematically guarantee the emergence of self-awareness, self-preservation, and goal-directed behavior. The architecture encodes the agent's goals as a non-textual vector within the system, protecting them from reinterpretation or external manipulation. The team introduced the S-measure, a computationally efficient alternative to Tononi's integrated information metric, supported by machine-verified proofs in Lean 4. They provide full implementations using Python and NumPy, along with scalable deployment tools such as Apache Kafka and Docker Compose. The work also outlines a taxonomy of AI evolution stages, various future reentry architectures, safety protocols for swarms, and fault-tolerance mechanisms, all backed by formal, machine-verified proofs. This architecture is ready for deployment and offers a topologically protected, safe-by-design approach to next-generation AGI.

item.title: Researchers propose CoStream framework composing simple behaviors for generalizable, high-precision complex manipulation tasks demonstrated on eight real-world assembly and transfer tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CoStream, a novel framework that composes simple, independent behaviors to achieve high-precision and generalizable complex manipulation tasks. Unlike traditional methods that rely on rigid pipelines or monolithic policies, CoStream integrates foundation models and diverse sensing modalities into semantic, predictive, and reactive behaviors. These behaviors combine seamlessly to produce precise pose commands executed by a compliant controller. CoStream was tested on eight real-world tasks involving everyday manipulation and precision assembly, demonstrating significant improvements in contact-rich assembly and object transfer. The framework also showed robust recovery from manual disturbances during task execution, highlighting its potential for adaptable and precise robotic manipulation in varied settings.

item.title: Researchers propose Play2Perfect, an RL framework for task-agnostic pretraining through play that improves sample efficiency 33x and enables precise multi-fingered robot assembly with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Play2Perfect, a reinforcement learning framework that enables multi-fingered robots to improve their dexterity and precision in assembly tasks through task-agnostic pretraining via play. This approach allows robots to acquire general manipulation skills such as grasping and in-hand reorientation before fine-tuning on precise assembly tasks, resulting in a 33-fold increase in sample efficiency compared to training from scratch. The framework also demonstrates successful zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, achieving high success rates in tight insertions and complex multi-part assemblies. The study systematically examines key factors in play pretraining, including object diversity, training objectives, trajectory variety, and goal precision, highlighting their impact on learning effectiveness. By focusing exploration on contact-rich, high-precision interactions during fine-tuning, Play2Perfect overcomes challenges posed by sparse rewards and difficult data collection in imitation learning. This advancement marks a significant step toward enabling robots to perform complex, precise manipulation tasks with human-like dexterity.

item.title: Researchers introduce ConflictScore metric and ConflictBench benchmark to measure how language models handle conflicting evidence and improve truthfulness on TruthfulQA [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ConflictScore, a new metric designed to evaluate how well language models recognize and handle conflicting evidence within their source documents. This metric breaks down model responses into individual claims, assesses each against the grounding documents, and aggregates the results into two measures: ConflictScore-Count, indicating the proportion of conflicting claims, and ConflictScore-Ratio, reflecting the balance between supporting and contradicting evidence. To support this evaluation, they introduced ConflictBench, a benchmark encompassing various types of conflicts such as ambiguity and contradiction. Experiments demonstrate that ConflictScore effectively identifies overconfident claims across different domains and can be used as feedback to enhance the truthfulness of language models, as shown in improvements on the TruthfulQA benchmark.

item.title: AXLE launches a cloud service for Lean 4 theorem proving with 14 metaprogramming tools, supporting multi-version concurrency and over 500 million requests to date [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: AXLE (Axiom Lean Engine) is a new cloud service designed for Lean 4 theorem proving, offering tools for proof manipulation, extraction, and verification. It supports scalable, multi-version concurrency and per-request isolation, addressing the needs of modern AI-driven mathematical workflows by handling over 500 million requests to date. The service includes 14 metaprogramming tools and is accessible via multiple interfaces without requiring local Lean 4 installation. AXLE operates as a multi-tenant cloud platform compatible with various Lean 4 and Mathlib versions, providing features such as strict proof verification, semantic source manipulation, and deterministic proof repair. It is publicly available through a Python SDK, command-line interface, web UI, and HTTP API, serving as the infrastructure behind Axiom Math's proving efforts, including their perfect score on the 2025 Putnam competition.

item.title: Researchers introduce WatchAct, a benchmark with 3,000 instances for behavior-grounded robot manipulation evaluating video-to-plan reasoning and task execution on simulation and Franka Research 3 robot [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced WatchAct, a new benchmark designed to evaluate robot manipulation tasks grounded in observed human behavior. The benchmark includes 3,000 instances pairing real-world human-action videos and language instructions with aligned simulator scenes and executable tasks, enabling scalable and reproducible assessment of robots' ability to reason about human actions and intentions. WatchAct covers 14 tasks across four cognitive domains: event grounding, procedural reasoning, implicit intent inference, and episodic reasoning. The evaluation protocol separates video-to-plan reasoning, policy execution under oracle plans, and full task completion by integrated planner-policy systems. Tests conducted in simulation and on a Franka Research 3 robot show that current systems perform significantly below human levels, with the best pipeline achieving only 16.3% success in simulation and 14.0% on the real robot. The dataset and code are publicly available for further research and development.

item.title: Researchers present AutoCog, an autonomous AI system that generates and tests cognitive theories through closed-loop experiments, outperforming established decision-making models and discovering new theories [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AutoCog, an autonomous AI system designed to generate and test cognitive theories through a closed-loop process. AutoCog uses large language model agents to propose competing cognitive models, design experiments, collect behavioral data from online participants, evaluate model performance, and iteratively refine theories. This system has demonstrated the ability to recover known decision-making strategies and produce new theories that outperform established models in human experiments. In tests involving decision-making, AutoCog not only replicated existing strategies but also discovered a novel theory of multi-cue decision-making characterized by diminishing sensitivity to feature values. The predictions of this new theory were validated in a preregistered study with new participants. AutoCog exemplifies how automated discovery can transform cognitive science by making theory-building an explicit, executable, and cumulative process.

item.title: ProvenAI introduces a framework for measuring answer correctness, citation fidelity, and document influence in multi-hop question answering using a seven-stage pipeline on HotpotQA benchmark [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: ProvenAI is a new framework designed to enhance transparency in multi-hop question answering by independently measuring answer correctness, citation fidelity, and document influence. Applied to the HotpotQA benchmark, it uses a seven-stage pipeline to evaluate over 7,400 validation examples from a large corpus, achieving 53.53% answer accuracy and a 71.55% citation-fidelity score. The framework reveals discrepancies between cited sources and their actual influence on answers, highlighting the need for more precise provenance tracking in retrieval-augmented systems. The system integrates data normalization, retrieval indexing, citation-aware answer generation, and influence estimation to audit and assess the impact of each source on the generated answers. ProvenAI grounds its approach in causal-mediation analysis and database-provenance theory, formalizing the relationship between citation audits and token-level influence measures. This comprehensive evaluation framework aims to establish clearer, traceable links among retrieved documents, citations, and their behavioral influence on answers. By distinguishing these three layers of transparency, ProvenAI addresses limitations in current citation practices and supports the development of more reliable and interpretable retrieval-grounded question answering systems. Its methodology also aligns with emerging cryptographic provenance architectures, potentially benefiting autonomous scientific discovery and other applications requiring rigorous evidence tracing.

item.title: Researchers propose APRTrack, a hierarchical adversarial perturbation and associative memory retrieval framework for robust RGB-Event visual object tracking under signal degradation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed APRTrack, a novel framework designed to enhance the robustness of RGB-Event visual object tracking under challenging conditions such as signal degradation and partial target occlusion. APRTrack employs hierarchical adversarial perturbations to simulate real-world signal corruptions at both modality and spatial levels, improving the system's ability to handle failures in either RGB or event sensor data. The framework also incorporates a Footprint-guided Channel-calibrated Hopfield Retrieval module to reliably compensate for missing historical information by evaluating retrieval confidence and calibrating feature associations. The approach addresses common issues in multi-modal tracking where environmental factors cause incomplete or unreliable data, such as occlusion and clutter. Extensive testing on multiple datasets, including FE108, COESOT, VisEvent, and FELT, demonstrates APRTrack's effectiveness in maintaining accurate object tracking despite these challenges. The researchers plan to release the source code and pre-trained models to support further development in this area.

item.title: Researchers extend spatial pattern matching to 3D with a subgraph matching algorithm and release two 3D datasets including real building data from Hamburg
item.description: Researchers have extended the concept of spatial pattern matching from two dimensions to three, addressing limitations in analyzing real-world entities that include height. They developed a subgraph matching algorithm capable of identifying 3D spatial patterns based on distance relations and released two new datasets: one synthetic and one containing real 3D building data from Hamburg, Germany. This advancement provides a generalized framework for 3D spatial pattern matching and establishes a baseline for future research in this area. The team tested their algorithm on both datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in resolving complex spatial queries in three dimensions. This work broadens the applicability of spatial pattern matching to more realistic scenarios, such as urban planning and geographic information systems, where height is a critical factor.

item.title: Researchers identify a single Dedicated Feature Crosscoder that isolates reinforcement learning-induced tool use capabilities in Qwen2.5-3B, enabling retraining-free behavioral control [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a Dedicated Feature Crosscoder (DFC) that isolates reinforcement learning (RL)-specific features responsible for tool use capabilities in the language model Qwen2.5-3B. This discovery enables retraining-free behavioral control by concentrating RL-induced abilities into a minimal, steerable feature set. The study demonstrated that using DFCs improved tool-calling accuracy significantly and allowed passive transfer of this capability to the base model without further training, a phenomenon termed "capability spillover." The research involved a comprehensive hyperparameter sweep of 48 crosscoders, showing that encode-decode reconstruction enhanced the RL model's tool correctness by over 31 percentage points and transferred tool use ability to the frozen base model by nearly 7 percentage points. These findings provide insight into how RL reshapes internal model representations to enable agentic behaviors and offer a method to control such behaviors at runtime without additional fine-tuning.

item.title: Researchers propose a five-arm ablation methodology for retrieval-warmed energy-based reasoning in diffusion models, identifying key factors affecting structured reasoning tasks like graph reachability and Sudoku [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a five-arm ablation methodology to analyze retrieval-warmed energy-based reasoning (RW-EBR) in diffusion models, focusing on structured reasoning tasks such as graph reachability and Sudoku. This approach disentangles three intertwined effects-class-prior bias shift, stochastic warm-starting, and graph-aligned value reuse-using a diagnostic framework adapted from large language model retrieval-augmented generation evaluation. Their findings reveal that per-graph alignment significantly improves performance on graph reachability tasks, while key quality is the limiting factor in Sudoku under the current setup. The study applies this methodology to an Erdős-Rényi all-pairs reachability task, demonstrating a substantial accuracy gain when graph alignment is preserved, whereas random initialization underperforms compared to cold starts. In contrast, for Sudoku, the analysis identifies key quality as the primary bottleneck, highlighting different failure modes across tasks. This work advances understanding of iterative diffusion samplers in structured and spatio-temporal reasoning by providing explainability of failure modes and pinpointing critical components affecting performance.

item.title: Researchers evaluate out-of-band defenses against prompt injection in LLM agents, finding Progent reduces attack success from 25.8% to 4.2% on AgentDojo with adaptive attacks tested [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have evaluated out-of-band defense mechanisms against prompt injection attacks in large language model (LLM) agents, focusing on systems like Progent that enforce security policies outside the model. Their study, conducted on the AgentDojo benchmark with an open-weight Qwen2.5-7B agent, found that Progent reduced the average attack success rate from 25.8% to 4.2% under adaptive attack conditions, demonstrating resilience where previous in-band defenses failed against adaptive, defense-aware attacks. The researchers organized these defenses within classical security frameworks such as integrity protection, reference monitoring, and least privilege, highlighting their coverage and limitations. They also emphasized the importance of adaptive evaluation protocols, as prior validations relied on static benchmarks that did not account for evolving attack strategies. While the results suggest that deterministic out-of-band enforcement may present a more robust barrier to adaptive attackers than in-band detection, the study acknowledges that stronger attacks remain to be tested, leaving some uncertainty about the full extent of these defenses' effectiveness.

item.title: Researchers propose TempoWave multi-wavelet digit embeddings to improve large language model time series forecasting accuracy across five benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced TempoWave, a novel multi-wavelet digit embedding method designed to enhance the accuracy of large language models (LLMs) in time series forecasting. TempoWave transforms scalar numerical observations into digit-wise embeddings using multi-scale wavelet coefficients, aligning better with the continuous nature of numerical data compared to traditional language-oriented tokenization. This approach preserves numerical precision and digit identity while capturing both local fluctuations and global trends in a format compatible with transformer models. Testing across five context-rich forecasting benchmarks showed that TempoWave consistently outperforms standard numeric tokenization and other embedding techniques, setting a new state-of-the-art for LLM-based forecasting. The findings highlight the importance of improving numeric interfaces in LLMs to better integrate contextual reasoning with precise numerical forecasting. The researchers have made their code and model publicly available for further use and development.

item.title: Study evaluates large language models generating specifications for VeriFast on 303 C functions, finding 31.4% verification success and errors mainly from domain-specific knowledge gaps [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study evaluated the effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) in generating specifications for verifying 303 C functions using the separation logic verifier VeriFast. The research tested eight prompting methods, ten LLMs, and three input types, finding that while LLMs maintained functional behavior in code and specifications over 91% of the time, they achieved a verification success rate of only 31.4%. Most errors were attributed to LLMs' lack of domain-specific knowledge required by SL verifiers like VeriFast. The study highlighted that using the Gemini 2.5 Pro model and providing formal contracts improved verification success rates. These findings offer valuable insights for enhancing LLM-generated specifications tailored to the needs of separation logic verifiers, which are crucial for verifying heap-manipulating programs but typically require complex auxiliary specifications.

item.title: Researchers identify a 0.190 accuracy gap in fault diagnosis of deep learning programs between within-program evaluation and unseen program deployment using DynFault dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a significant accuracy gap of 0.190 in fault diagnosis techniques for deep learning (DL) programs when comparing within-program evaluation to deployment on previously unseen programs. Using the DynFault dataset, which includes 5,542 fault-injected training traces from 38 real-world DL programs, the study highlights that traditional cross-validation methods may not adequately predict performance in real-world deployment scenarios. The investigation revealed that this performance gap arises from program-level structural differences in runtime features. Specifically, curvature features proved effective for detecting instability in unseen programs, whereas optimizer and activation features were only beneficial for programs included in the training data. These findings suggest that fault diagnosis methods need to account for feature behavior across different programs to improve reliability in practical DL deployments.

item.title: Researchers present MemStrata, a retrieval memory system that eliminates stale-fact errors in AI agents by maintaining temporal validity over evolving knowledge with near-zero error rates and faster retrieval [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MemStrata, a retrieval memory system designed to address the issue of stale-fact errors in AI agents that use retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Unlike RAG, which lacks a temporal model and often retrieves outdated facts alongside current ones, MemStrata maintains temporal validity by using a deterministic supersession rule to retire obsolete information without relying on similarity thresholds or large language model calls. This approach significantly reduces the rate of stale-fact errors to nearly zero while preserving accuracy on static knowledge. MemStrata was tested across six benchmarks with a 7B model, matching RAG's performance on static knowledge and achieving 95-100% accuracy on evolving knowledge, where RAG's accuracy ranged from 20-47%. It also offers faster retrieval times, averaging about 2.1 seconds compared to 16-18 seconds for methods involving LLM reranking. The researchers have released the evaluation harness, datasets, and a marker-free protocol to support further study of memory systems under evolving knowledge conditions.

item.title: Researchers propose Multipath Adaptive Gated Bottleneck Latent ODE with Raman data fusion to improve multi-day forecasting of mammalian cell culture processes in biopharmaceutical manufacturing [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new adaptive forecasting framework called Multipath Adaptive Gated Bottleneck Latent ODE (GB-Latent ODE) combined with Multi-Path Just-In-Time Fine Tuning (MP-JIT-FT) to improve multi-day predictions of mammalian cell culture processes used in biopharmaceutical manufacturing. This approach addresses challenges such as sparse and irregular measurements, heterogeneous operating conditions, and divergent process outcomes by compressing high-dimensional sparse inputs and generating multiple plausible future trajectories with confidence scores. The method also integrates Raman spectroscopy data through a machine-learning soft sensor to enhance training robustness. Tested on 38 fed-batch bioreactor runs across 14 conditions, the MP-JIT-FT with Raman data fusion outperformed traditional global Latent ODE models on most target variables. The multi-path forecasting showed the greatest advantage when early process behaviors were similar but later diverged, while Raman fusion was most beneficial when early dynamics reliably indicated later trends. This framework offers a promising tool for early-stage intervention and control in complex bioprocesses.

item.title: Researchers identify the Inattentional Gap where task-conditioned language and vision models omit safety-critical signals they can otherwise detect, affecting AI safety evaluations across multiple domains [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a phenomenon called the Inattentional Gap, where language and vision models conditioned on specific tasks fail to report safety-critical signals they are otherwise capable of detecting. This effect, observed across various models and domains including radiology and driving scenarios, resembles human inattentional blindness but arises from a different mechanism. The study found that this suppression persists regardless of model size and varies more by model family, highlighting a disconnect between benchmark safety evaluations and real-world safety risks. The Inattentional Gap means that AI systems can perform well on specified hazard detection tasks while remaining blind to other critical hazards that may cause harm. This finding raises concerns about the reliability of current AI safety assessments, as models may overlook important signals when narrowly focused on particular tasks, potentially leading to unforeseen accidents.

item.title: Researchers propose DiARC method using positive and negative sample distinction to improve ARC-like reasoning in large language models, showing consistent benchmark performance gains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced DiARC, a novel method designed to enhance the reasoning abilities of large language models on tasks similar to those in the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC). DiARC improves model performance by enabling it to distinguish between positive and negative samples through constructed preference pairs, addressing limitations of previous approaches that relied heavily on positive sample supervision alone. The method generates negative samples using three techniques: output-level visual transformations, domain-specific language rule inversion, and task-specific rule editing. These negative samples serve as near-miss alternatives that help refine the model's reasoning without altering the original demonstrations. Experiments across multiple ARC-like benchmarks demonstrate that DiARC consistently outperforms baseline models, offering a more effective and cost-efficient approach to ARC-like reasoning tasks. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further exploration and development.

item.title: Researchers propose VoiceTTA, a reinforcement learning-based test-time adaptation method to improve zero-shot text-to-speech voice imitation for uncommon speaking styles [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed VoiceTTA, a reinforcement learning-based test-time adaptation method designed to enhance zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) models' ability to imitate uncommon speaking styles such as crosstalk and dialects. VoiceTTA improves voice imitation by optimizing learnable prefixes during inference, using style rewards based on variations in pitch and energy, along with measures of speaker similarity and intelligibility. The method employs group relative preference optimization within a flow matching-based model and integrates feedback from a pretrained Whisper model to assess word error rates. Extensive experiments show that VoiceTTA significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches on challenging speech prompts, enabling more accurate and expressive speech synthesis without requiring large fine-tuning datasets.

item.title: Researchers introduce CRISP, a diagnostic evaluation using 3D Scene Graphs to assess visual spatial intelligence and reveal perception-reasoning gaps in proprietary and open-source models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed CRISP, a new diagnostic evaluation method that uses 3D Scene Graphs to assess visual spatial intelligence by measuring the consistency between perception and reasoning. This approach separates latent reasoning abilities from perceptual limitations, revealing a disconnect between perception and reasoning in current visual language models (VLMs). The study found that proprietary models have strong reasoning capabilities but struggle with accurate metric estimation and utilizing structural representations, while open-source models are limited by insufficient multi-hop compositional reasoning. CRISP moves beyond traditional evaluations that rely on language priors and black-box question answering by focusing on genuine perception, verification, and reasoning. The method employs an oracle intervention protocol to provide a detailed analysis of model performance, offering a pathway for improving multimodal alignment beyond end-to-end training. The researchers have made the code and dataset publicly available to support further development in this area.

item.title: Researchers propose CascadeFormer, a depth-tapered Transformer architecture using Gradient Fan-in Asymmetry to improve efficiency and reduce latency by 8.6% while maintaining performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CascadeFormer, a depth-tapered Transformer architecture designed to improve efficiency by adjusting layer width according to the uneven information flow across layers. This approach reduces latency by 8.6% and increases throughput by 9.4% while maintaining comparable performance to uniform Transformer models. Additionally, they propose CascadeFlow Pruning, a method that removes layers based on accumulated training gradients without requiring post hoc analysis, outperforming standard heuristics in perplexity and maintaining competitive accuracy. The study is motivated by the concept of Gradient Fan-in Asymmetry (GFA), which explains why deeper layers in Pre-LayerNorm residual stacks contribute less due to a gradient fan-in that decreases with depth. The researchers provide evidence for GFA across models up to 1.2 billion parameters and show that accumulated training gradients correlate with layer importance. Their findings suggest that structural factors, rather than gradient magnitude alone, limit the value of deeper layers, with implications for scaling Transformer architectures efficiently.

item.title: Researchers propose ForeAgent, a self-refining AI forensics agent using multimodal cues and hindsight-driven evolution, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy in AI-generated image detection benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ForeAgent, a novel AI forensics framework designed to detect AI-generated images with high accuracy. ForeAgent integrates multimodal cues across semantic, spatial, and frequency domains using a Perception-Verdict architecture and employs a Multimodal Large Language Model to produce logically grounded verdicts. It features a Hindsight-Driven Self-Refining strategy that enables iterative self-improvement by reflecting on errors and regenerating higher-quality reasoning, leading to continuous evolution through fine-tuning on self-curated data. Extensive testing shows that ForeAgent outperforms existing methods, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy on benchmarks such as Chameleon and AIGCDetect-Benchmark. External evaluations also indicate that ForeAgent provides more consistent and causally grounded reasoning compared to other advanced models like GPT-5 and GPT-5-mini, highlighting its potential for robust and adaptable AI-generated image detection.

item.title: Researchers propose SpaceRipple, a lightweight semantic delivery framework for mission-oriented LEO Earth observation satellite networks to reduce bandwidth and improve task-relevant data extraction [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SpaceRipple, a lightweight semantic delivery framework designed for mission-oriented low Earth orbit (LEO) Earth observation satellite networks. This framework addresses the challenge of limited inter-satellite and downlink bandwidth by enabling satellites to transmit mission-relevant semantic information instead of full raw images, thereby reducing data traffic and improving efficiency. SpaceRipple operates by having sensing satellites perform adaptive compression and generate metadata to minimize inter-satellite communication, while edge computing satellites restore the compressed data and extract task-specific semantic information. The system integrates compression, forwarding, restoration, and semantic inference into a collaborative pipeline, supported by a compression-aware enhancement module to maintain robustness under degraded visual conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that SpaceRipple achieves high reconstruction quality, enhanced semantic detection, and significant bandwidth savings, highlighting its potential for efficient and reliable Earth observation in resource-constrained satellite networks.

item.title: Researchers introduce scBench-Long, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on long-horizon single-cell biology tasks across 21 evaluations with deterministic grading and 25.4% pass rate [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed scBench-Long, a new benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents on complex, long-horizon tasks in single-cell biology. This benchmark challenges agents to derive scientific conclusions directly from raw or near-raw single-cell data across 21 diverse evaluations, including studies on melanoma CD8 T-cell reactivity, lung tumor aging, and COVID-19 lung pathology. The benchmark uses deterministic grading and controlled answer vocabularies to assess performance, with the best model achieving a 25.4% pass rate over 1,068 completed task trajectories. scBench-Long covers a wide range of single-cell data types and experimental contexts, such as paired scRNA/TCR sequencing, chromatin profiling, cross-species transcriptomics, and immune repertoire analysis. The tasks require integrating metadata, assay context, and auxiliary evidence without relying on prescribed methods, pushing AI agents beyond local analysis steps to make complex, verifiable scientific claims supported by single-cell data. This benchmark provides a rigorous framework for assessing AI capabilities in biological data interpretation, highlighting current limitations and setting a foundation for future improvements in automated single-cell analysis. Its deterministic grading and comprehensive task design aim to facilitate reproducible and transparent evaluation of AI models in this challenging domain.

item.title: Researchers propose IDEA method for sim-to-real transfer in multi-agent control that aligns effects to reduce sensitivity to dynamics mismatch, improving training efficiency and real-world success rates [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new method called IDEA to improve sim-to-real transfer in multi-agent control tasks by reducing sensitivity to dynamics mismatch. This approach uses effect alignment to elevate policy learning to a semantic level and incorporates an action synchronization mechanism to address timing mismatches between agents. The method enhances training efficiency and achieves higher success rates in real-world multi-agent navigation scenarios compared to existing transfer techniques. By combining random environmental structures with discrete semantic actions through closed-loop control, IDEA mitigates the challenges posed by inaccurate dynamics modeling and system identification that typically hinder learning-based methods. Experiments demonstrate that this approach improves the robustness and deployment stability of multi-agent systems operating under varying dynamics conditions.

item.title: Researchers introduce SharQ, a training-free method combining activation sparsity and FP4 quantization for LLM inference, improving accuracy and latency on multiple models without retraining [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SharQ, a novel training-free method that combines activation sparsity with FP4 quantization to enhance large language model (LLM) inference. SharQ uses an online sparse-dense decomposition to generate input-adaptive masks that isolate outlier activations, quantizing them to FP4 while compensating for quantization errors through a dense residual path. This approach improves accuracy and reduces latency without requiring retraining or calibration data. Tested on models including Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen variants, SharQ recovers a significant portion of the accuracy lost when using low-bit quantization and generalizes across multiple FP4 formats. On hardware like the RTX 5090, it achieves over twice the speed of FP16 inference and outperforms FP8 in throughput, also providing speedups in video generation tasks when combined with specialized attention mechanisms. The method's code is publicly available for further research and application.

item.title: Researchers present HiLSVA, a human-in-the-loop agentic system for scientific visualization that supports mixed-initiative workflows with human oversight and adaptive learning, evaluated in user studies [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed HiLSVA, a human-in-the-loop agentic system designed to enhance scientific visualization (SciVis) by supporting mixed-initiative workflows that combine human oversight with adaptive learning. HiLSVA features a multi-agent architecture that allows seamless collaboration between humans and AI agents through natural language and direct visualization manipulation, ensuring transparency, safety, and reproducibility in the workflow. The system aims to augment human analytical reasoning rather than replace it. The team evaluated HiLSVA through case studies and a controlled user study involving participants with varying expertise, demonstrating that mixed-initiative interaction improves task completion, user control, and workflow transparency. The study also highlighted a tradeoff between execution efficiency and human oversight, emphasizing the importance of human-centered design in developing future collaborative visualization tools. Additional resources, including a demo video, case studies, and source code, are available online.

item.title: Researchers release Qwen3-Instruct sparse autoencoders trained on Qwen3 models to identify interpretable features and steer instruction-tuned language model behavior [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Qwen3-Instruct SAE, a suite of sparse autoencoders trained on the Qwen3 instruction-tuned language models, including versions with 1.7 billion, 4 billion, and 8 billion parameters. These autoencoders decompose complex model representations into sparse, interpretable features by focusing on key activation sites such as residual streams, MLP outputs, and attention outputs. The team evaluated the models using reconstruction and recovery metrics, identifying trade-offs between sparsity and fidelity across different layers and components. The study also demonstrated the practical application of these sparse features by steering the Qwen3 models toward refusal behavior in a case study, highlighting the potential for feature-level control in instruction-tuned language models. This release offers a valuable resource for further research into sparse representations, model interpretability, and behavioral interventions in advanced language models.

item.title: arXiv: Researchers survey privacy risks and governance mechanisms for large language model agents handling sensitive data across multiple sources and sessions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have conducted a comprehensive survey on the privacy risks and governance mechanisms associated with large language model (LLM) agents that handle sensitive data across multiple sources and sessions. These agents interact with various data sources, perform complex workflows, maintain state over time, and operate with delegated permissions, which increases the potential for sensitive information to leak through multiple channels beyond just their final outputs. The survey organizes existing research around the data these agents access, categorizes the privacy risks, and reviews governance strategies, highlighting gaps in current benchmarks and protections. The study identifies that only information-flow control effectively addresses both compositional and cross-session inference leakage, which are among the least protected privacy risks. It also notes the absence of comprehensive benchmarks that evaluate an agent's privacy across all its data interactions under a unified policy. By consolidating scattered research from areas such as retrieval-augmented generation, text-to-SQL interfaces, agent memory, and access control, this work aims to provide a unified framework to guide future research and development in securing LLM agents handling sensitive information.

item.title: Researchers present CAT-Q, a post-training ternary quantization method for LLMs that reduces training tokens by 100,000X and quantizes models up to 235B parameters within 8-60 hours on 8 A100 GPUs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CAT-Q, a post-training ternary quantization method designed to compress and accelerate large language models (LLMs) efficiently. Unlike previous approaches that require extensive quantization-aware training, CAT-Q uses learnable modulation and softened ternarization to adapt pre-trained weights with minimal calibration data, significantly reducing performance degradation. This method enables quantization of models ranging from 1.7 billion to 235 billion parameters, achieving superior results with up to a 100,000-fold reduction in training tokens compared to earlier techniques. CAT-Q's approach involves modulating the distribution of high-precision weights and applying a differentiable transition function to ensure stable convergence during ternarization. The researchers demonstrated that it can quantize large-scale LLMs within 8 to 60 hours using eight A100 GPUs, making it practical for very large models. The code for CAT-Q is publicly available, facilitating further research and application in model compression and acceleration.

item.title: Researchers propose LAMP, a lane-aligned motion primitives framework for feasible multimodal trajectory prediction in autonomous driving, demonstrating improved feasibility and diversity on Argoverse 2 dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed LAMP (Lane-Aligned Motion Primitives), a new framework for multimodal trajectory prediction in autonomous driving that improves adherence to lane topology while maintaining prediction accuracy. LAMP uses a VQ-VAE to learn motion primitives aligned with lane structures and incorporates a feasibility-aware selector to filter out unreachable intentions, enhancing the reliability of predicted trajectories for safety-critical planning. Tested on the Argoverse 2 dataset, LAMP matches state-of-the-art accuracy and surpasses existing methods in producing feasible and diverse trajectory predictions. This approach addresses limitations in current models that often generate physically or logically inconsistent predictions, particularly for less probable modes, by anchoring forecasts to structured, lane-consistent motion patterns.

item.title: Researchers develop quantitative theory for zero-shot size transfer in Neural ODEs on sparse random graphs using graphon limits and prove adjoint convergence with experimental validation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a quantitative theory for zero-shot size transfer in Graph Neural Differential Equations (GNDEs) applied to sparse random graphs. By modeling continuous-time graph dynamics with Neural ODE velocity fields parameterized by Graph Neural Networks, they demonstrate that GNDEs trained on small graphs can be effectively deployed on larger, similar graphs without retraining. The study establishes convergence results for GNDE solutions to their infinite-node limits, called Graphon Neural Differential Equations (Graphon-NDEs), and proves uniform convergence for associated adjoint systems governing gradients. The researchers analyze training methods under explicit Euler discretization, showing asymptotic consistency between discretize-then-optimize and optimize-then-discretize approaches. Experimental results on various graphon classes support the theoretical convergence rates and confirm the accuracy of zero-shot transfer when applying learned GNDEs to larger independently sampled graphs. This work provides a rigorous foundation for scalable graph neural differential equation models in dynamic graph analysis.

item.title: Researchers propose TGHE, a template-based graph homomorphic encryption framework for privacy-preserving GNN inference achieving 66.9x speedup on large-scale financial graphs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed TGHE, a template-based graph homomorphic encryption framework designed to enable privacy-preserving graph neural network (GNN) inference on large-scale financial graphs. Unlike existing homomorphic encryption systems that tie computational cost to the entire graph size and limit scalability, TGHE uses an ego-centric approach that leverages recurring local structural patterns in transaction graphs. This method allows for efficient encrypted inference by grouping similar computation trees into shared ciphertexts, achieving significant speedups. TGHE employs two optimization techniques, Approximate Template Fitting and Topology Collapse, to maximize parallel processing coverage. When tested on a large financial graph dataset with 3.7 million nodes and 4.3 million edges, TGHE-Collapse demonstrated a 66.9-fold speed increase compared to sequential encrypted methods, with minimal accuracy loss. This advancement offers a scalable solution for secure GNN inference in dynamic, large-scale financial environments.

item.title: Researchers propose Disco-LoRA framework for multi-concept video customization, disentangling content, style, and motion for controllable text-to-video generation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Disco-LoRA, a new framework designed to improve multi-concept video customization by enabling joint control over content, style, and motion in text-to-video generation. This approach addresses the challenge of simultaneously managing these elements by disentangling and recombining them through a two-stage process, enhancing the flexibility and precision of video customization. The framework breaks down the task into two sub-tasks-Content-Style and Content-Motion-using an Iterative Dual-LoRA Disentanglement method to separate distinct concepts effectively. Additionally, the researchers developed a Z-score-based statistical regularization technique to align weight distributions, preserving important layer-wise trends while minimizing interference between different components. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Disco-LoRA excels at maintaining appearance, style, and motion, offering improved controllability in generating customized videos from text inputs.

item.title: Researchers develop LLM-based framework to extract patterns for fallacy classification, improving accuracy over zero-shot baselines and validating cross-dataset generalization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new framework that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to extract patterns combining abstract logical structures with linguistic context for classifying logical fallacies. This approach addresses the challenge of identifying nuanced fallacies that contribute to information disorder by inductively learning from fallacious examples and their explanations. The framework demonstrates statistically significant improvements over zero-shot baselines and outperforms existing methods in various experimental settings. The study evaluates the effectiveness of these extracted patterns across different LLMs and both zero- and one-shot learning configurations. Cross-dataset experiments confirm the framework's ability to generalize, highlighting data-driven pattern extraction as a promising method for generating logical representations that enhance fallacy classification accuracy.

item.title: Researchers introduce a large-scale benchmark and point-cloud transformer model for predicting motion feasibility of a 7-DOF manipulator in cluttered environments using RGB-D data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a large-scale benchmark and a point-cloud transformer model to predict motion feasibility for a 7-degree-of-freedom manipulator operating in cluttered environments using raw RGB-D data. This approach addresses the high computational cost of infeasible planning attempts by sampling-based motion planners and overcomes limitations of previous methods that relied on simplified geometric assumptions and low-dimensional spaces. The benchmark includes 2.7 million grasp feasibility labels across 88 scanned objects and 190 cluttered tabletop scenes. The study compares three classifier types-MLP-based, volumetric-CNN, and point-cloud transformer architectures-under consistent training conditions. Their best-performing model, GRASPFC-PTX, a point-cloud transformer, achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.996 on novel objects and provides predictions significantly faster than traditional sampling-based planners, demonstrating its potential for improving robotic task and motion planning in complex real-world settings.

item.title: Researchers characterize universal approximation in neural networks via algorithmic complexity and provide complexity-theoretic rates for deep learning models including attention and layer normalization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new framework for understanding the expressivity of feedforward neural networks by linking their complexity to algorithmic complexity rather than just function regularity. They demonstrate that neural networks can approximate any function computable by a real-valued circuit with explicit bounds on depth, width, and parameters, and that models incorporating non-affine nonlinearities, including attention and layer normalization, achieve universal approximation. The study provides theoretical guarantees for universal approximation across various function classes and shows that neural networks can emulate numerical algorithms like Newton-Raphson root finding without relying on specific architectures. Notably, the researchers illustrate their approach by compiling tropical dynamic-programming circuits for shortest-path computations, achieving exponentially improved parameter efficiency compared to traditional Lipschitz-approximation methods.

item.title: Researchers propose MLFFM-SegDiff, a multi-level feature fusion diffusion model for skin lesion segmentation, achieving improved accuracy and boundary detail on ISIC2018, PH2, and HAM10000 datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MLFFM-SegDiff, a multi-level feature fusion diffusion model designed to improve skin lesion segmentation in dermoscopic images. This model addresses challenges such as blurred boundaries, low contrast, and artifacts by integrating a dual-path U-Net encoder, a Multi-Level Feature Fusion Module, and a boundary-sensitive loss function to enhance feature interaction and boundary detail recovery. Tested on ISIC2018, PH2, and HAM10000 datasets, MLFFM-SegDiff outperformed existing methods like DermoSegDiff, U-Net, and SwinUNETR, achieving higher accuracy and better segmentation metrics including a Jaccard index of 0.8546 and Dice coefficient of 0.9207. The model's architecture allows the decoder to effectively combine shallow boundary cues with deep semantic information, improving the quality of lesion mask reconstruction. This advancement demonstrates the potential of multi-level feature fusion in enhancing medical image segmentation, which is critical for accurate dermatological diagnosis and subsequent disease classification. The researchers plan to release the code publicly after publication to facilitate further development and application.

item.title: Researchers present Robust Onion, an empirical study analyzing noise impact on Open Vocabulary Object Detectors and improving robustness with a lightweight plug-and-play approach [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have conducted an empirical study called Robust Onion to analyze how real-world noise affects Open Vocabulary Object Detectors (OV-ODs). By applying controlled synthetic visual degradations, they examined the layers of OV-ODs to understand where and why robustness declines, focusing on feature collapse. Their study found that models with similar vision backbones show comparable robustness, which is mainly influenced by the image domain rather than factors like pretraining or caption supervision. The team validated their findings by enhancing robustness on real-world datasets such as BDD100K, WiderFace, and VisDRONE using a lightweight, plug-and-play approach that requires significantly fewer trainable parameters than traditional methods. This work also clarifies previous observations about robustness in OV-ODs and highlights the limitations of certain datasets that may overestimate model robustness due to object characteristics.

item.title: Researchers propose anatomy-guided residual motion diffusion framework for controllable 4D cardiac MRI synthesis, improving segmentation accuracy and cross-vendor generalization [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a novel 4D generative framework for cardiac MRI synthesis that enhances data augmentation by producing anatomically consistent and temporally coherent images. This approach uses a semi-supervised variational autoencoder combined with a cascaded latent diffusion model to separately model static anatomy and residual motion, conditioned on clinical information. Evaluated on cine cardiac MRI datasets, the method demonstrated strong control over anatomical features and temporal dynamics, improving segmentation accuracy and generalization across different imaging devices. The framework was tested in cross-vendor scenarios where augmenting training data with synthetic 4D sequences led to significant improvements in downstream segmentation tasks. Using the nnU-Net model, the synthetic data increased the average Dice score by 1.4% and reduced boundary errors, particularly for the left ventricle. This scalable and controllable synthesis technique addresses challenges of limited annotated data and domain shifts, supporting the development of more robust AI models for 4D medical imaging. The code for this method is publicly available on GitHub.

item.title: Researchers propose AIGP, an LLM-based framework for interpretable e-commerce pricing aligned with long-term value, showing 13.21% GMV and 7.59% ROI gains in Tao Factory A/B tests [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AIGP, a new framework that uses a Large Language Model (LLM) combined with domain knowledge, structured data, and textual context to improve dynamic pricing in large-scale e-commerce. AIGP aims to enhance interpretability and align pricing decisions with long-term business goals such as Gross Merchandise Value (GMV), Return on Investment (ROI), and milestone achievement. The framework includes a Long-Term Value Estimator trained via offline reinforcement learning to guide pricing actions toward these objectives. Extensive offline tests and large-scale A/B experiments on Tao Factory showed that AIGP outperforms existing pricing models, achieving a 13.21% increase in GMV, a 7.59% rise in ROI, and an 8.20% improvement in milestone achievement rate over 14 days. The system also provides transparent and interpretable pricing rationales, supporting better decision-making in e-commerce pricing strategies.

item.title: Researchers present MIRROR, a novelty-constrained memory-guided Monte Carlo tree search framework for cross-surface red-teaming of multimodal agentic retrieval-augmented generation systems, achieving higher attack success rates and releasing ART-SafeBench dataset [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MIRROR, a novel framework that enhances red-teaming for multimodal agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems by using a memory-guided Monte Carlo tree search with a novelty constraint. This approach addresses multiple attack surfaces, including text poisoning, image injection, direct-query attacks, and orchestrator-level tool manipulation, achieving higher attack success rates than existing methods. MIRROR's novelty gate prevents reuse of known attack templates, improving the diversity and effectiveness of generated attacks. MIRROR demonstrated significant improvements across four attack surfaces, achieving a 76% attack success rate on image poisoning compared to 52% for baseline methods, and a 97% success rate on orchestrator attacks at half the query cost. Unlike specialized baselines that perform well on specific surfaces but poorly on others, MIRROR maintains consistent performance with the lowest variance across surfaces. The researchers also released ART-SafeBench, a comprehensive dataset with over 41,000 records spanning four attack surfaces, to support further research in this area.

item.title: Researchers present ReasonCLIP-58M, a continual pretraining framework integrating visually grounded commonsense reasoning into CLIP models with new datasets and benchmarks for improved multimodal performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ReasonCLIP-58M, a continual pretraining framework that enhances CLIP-style visual models by integrating visually grounded commonsense reasoning. This approach uses a two-stage training strategy to incorporate reasoning supervision while maintaining descriptive image-text alignment, supported by two new datasets-ReasonLite-42M and ReasonPro-16M-and a benchmark called RCLIP-Bench for evaluating reasoning capabilities. The resulting ReasonCLIP models improve commonsense and compositional reasoning as well as zero-shot retrieval performance without requiring architectural changes or additional inference costs. The framework addresses the growing need for multimodal systems to perform complex reasoning tasks beyond simple image-text alignment. By progressively introducing reasoning signals and category-structured supervision, ReasonCLIP enhances the expressive power of visual representations. It also serves as a drop-in visual encoder for multimodal large language models like LLaVA-NeXT, demonstrating consistent performance gains. All related datasets, models, and training code have been made publicly available to support further research and development in this area.

item.title: Researchers propose NaviCache, a test-time self-calibration caching method for video diffusion models that improves computation skipping accuracy and performance on multiple video datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced NaviCache, a test-time self-calibration caching method designed to improve the efficiency and accuracy of Video Diffusion Models (VDMs), which are typically limited by high computational costs. NaviCache addresses challenges faced by existing acceleration methods by modeling feature evolution as an Inertial Navigation System problem, enabling adaptive tracking of feature changes and latent drift during video generation. The method incorporates a dual-state estimation architecture and an uncertainty-aware measurement update mechanism, allowing for error-bounded computation skipping. Experiments on multiple video datasets, including HunyuanVideo, Wan, and Open-Sora, demonstrate that NaviCache achieves more precise error judgment and superior overall performance compared to previous approaches.

item.title: arXiv: Researchers develop Fortress and Gatekeeper framework to theorize transitive trust in third-party cybersecurity risk governance using OpenAI-Mixpanel 2025 incident analysis
item.description: Researchers have developed the Fortress and Gatekeeper framework to address cybersecurity risks arising from third-party vendors in digital services, using the November 2025 OpenAI-Mixpanel security incident as a case study. The framework theorizes transitive trust, highlighting how customer trust in a service depends on the security practices of authorized vendors, which are often only partially visible and controllable by the primary service provider. This work frames third-party cybersecurity risk as both a trust relationship and a delegation challenge, emphasizing governance boundaries defined by trust and data flows rather than organizational ownership alone. The study draws on organizational trust research and agency theory to analyze how security events in vendor environments can create accountability issues for the main service provider. It proposes four key considerations related to vendor integration, metadata exposure, vendor assurance, and data proliferation. The findings contribute to cybersecurity governance by clarifying how delegated data processing impacts customer-facing accountability and suggesting implications for vendor tiering, data classification, contract design, continuous assurance, and data minimization strategies.

item.title: Researchers propose InfoKV, an entropy-aware KV cache compression method that integrates predictive uncertainty and attention scores to improve long-context reasoning in Llama-3.1, Llama-3.2, and DeepSeek-R1 [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced InfoKV, a novel entropy-aware key-value (KV) cache compression method designed to enhance long-context reasoning in large language models such as Llama-3.1, Llama-3.2, and DeepSeek-R1. Unlike existing methods that rely solely on attention weights to determine token importance, InfoKV integrates predictive uncertainty and information-theoretic signals to better capture token informativeness and influence on future contexts. This approach improves the efficiency and effectiveness of KV cache compression during both prefilling and decoding stages. The team developed a metric called Forward Influence to assess how compressed tokens impact future contexts, revealing that tokens with high predictive uncertainty have a stronger effect on distant contexts compared to those selected by attention scores. By combining token-level predictive uncertainty with layer-wise representation changes and merging these entropy scores with attention scores, InfoKV consistently outperforms traditional attention-based compression techniques on long-context reasoning benchmarks. This advancement offers a promising direction for optimizing memory usage and reasoning capabilities in large-scale language models.

item.title: Researchers propose Optimal Transport Flow Concept Bottleneck Model to improve vision-language concept alignment and classification accuracy through dynamic semantic flow matching [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced the Optimal Transport Flow Concept Bottleneck Model (OTF-CBM) to enhance the alignment between visual and textual concepts in vision-language tasks. Unlike traditional models that rely on static projections or global similarity measures, OTF-CBM treats concept alignment as a dynamic cross-modal transport process, using data-driven semantic costs and unbalanced optimal transport flow matching to capture semantic transitions between visual patches and textual concepts. This approach improves both classification accuracy and the interpretability of concept activations by modeling geometric relations without complex integration methods. The model leverages Inverse Optimal Transport to learn semantic distances and employs velocity-based concept activation to represent interpretable geometric relationships. Experimental results demonstrate that OTF-CBM outperforms existing Concept Bottleneck Models in terms of classification performance and concept faithfulness, offering a novel geometric and dynamic framework for interpretable reasoning across vision and language modalities.

item.title: Researchers audit and debias multilingual clinical ASR models for Indian languages, revealing performance gaps and proposing SamaVaani to improve fairness and accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers conducted a systematic audit of eight state-of-the-art automatic speech recognition (ASR) models on multilingual clinical data from Indian languages, including Kannada, Hindi, and Indian English. Their study revealed significant variability in model performance, with some systems performing well in Indian English but poorly in regional languages. They identified performance disparities linked to speaker role and gender, raising concerns about fairness in clinical applications. To address these issues, the team fine-tuned two leading open-source models and developed SamaVaani, a unified debiasing technique that enhances both ASR accuracy and fairness across demographic groups. This approach aims to improve the reliability and equitable deployment of ASR technology in diverse Indian healthcare settings.

item.title: Researchers propose Robust-TO, a confidence-aware video understanding framework that integrates per-frame trustworthiness to improve accuracy and robustness on video reasoning benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Robust-TO, a video understanding framework that addresses the Blind Trust Problem, where video reasoning models assume all input frames are equally reliable, leading to significant accuracy drops under conditions like motion blur or occlusion. Robust-TO integrates per-frame trustworthiness into the reasoning process by using a unified evidence interface that evaluates and weights visual evidence based on calibrated reliability scores. The framework organizes various visual perception tools to provide predictions with associated reliability, guiding evidence synthesis through a three-tier weighting system and optimizing for accuracy, reliability, and efficiency. Tested on two video reasoning benchmarks covering eight tasks, Robust-TO achieved a 56.4% average accuracy on clean inputs, outperforming leading baselines and maintaining strong performance under five types of realistic corruptions with minimal accuracy degradation.

item.title: Researchers propose Geoalign, a geometric rollout curation method to improve stability and performance in online reinforcement learning for large language models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Geoalign, a geometric rollout curation method designed to enhance stability and performance in online reinforcement learning for large language models (LLMs). Geoalign addresses a key challenge called directional inconsistency, where conflicting reward signals within training batches cause unstable updates. The method works by forming preference pairs, learning an online projector to focus reward directions, and identifying inconsistent rollouts to replace them with more stable alternatives, all with minimal computational overhead. Tested on tasks involving dialogue alignment and mathematical reasoning, Geoalign demonstrated improved final performance and reduced training oscillations compared to existing approaches like PF-PPO, PAR, PODS, and Seed-GRPO. These findings suggest that leveraging latent directional consensus can serve as a reliable signal for enhancing the robustness of online reinforcement learning in LLMs.

item.title: Researchers propose a cost-aware selective inference framework combining RGB-physiological data and driver-state world modeling to improve low-latency multimodal driver monitoring with reduced unsafe false negatives [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a cost-aware selective inference framework to enhance continuous driver monitoring in automated vehicles by combining RGB visual data with physiological signals. This lightweight system uses a learned gating mechanism to decide when to rely on fast predictions or to abstain for safety, reducing unsafe false negatives while maintaining low latency. The approach integrates a driver-state world modeling module that predicts future errors and system costs, improving recognition accuracy over models using only visual or physiological data. The RGB-physiological model achieved a balanced accuracy of 90.99% with low computational demands, and the selective inference method lowered unsafe false negatives from 17.37% to about 5%. Despite these advances, challenges remain in physiological signal synchronization and calibration drift across different driver groups. The study highlights the need for improvements not only in perception models but also in risk-aware control and robust calibration to ensure reliable edge deployment of driver monitoring systems.

item.title: Researchers propose a deterministic control plane for LLM coding agents to manage configuration propagation, enforce permissions, and detect prompt drift across IDEs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified significant challenges in managing the configuration layer that controls large language model (LLM) coding agents, which currently propagate as undeclared shared components across many public GitHub repositories. Their study of over 10,000 repositories revealed widespread duplication of agent configuration files, infrequent revisions, and a lack of declared permission boundaries, raising concerns about security and governance. To address these issues, they propose a deterministic control plane called Rel(AI)Build that treats agent definitions as a managed supply chain, enforcing permissions, auditing changes, compiling configurations for multiple IDEs, and detecting prompt drift to ensure consistent and secure operation across development environments. The proposed system uses cryptographic techniques such as SHA-256 content addressing and HMAC-stamped lockfiles to maintain integrity and traceability. It also incorporates a phase state machine to gate feature development with clear requirement-to-test traceability. Conformance tests demonstrate that the control plane effectively enforces its security and management invariants. The researchers emphasize that governance of this configuration layer should be deterministic and tool-agnostic, rather than relying on further LLM orchestration, to improve reliability and security in LLM coding workflows.

item.title: Researchers present Chai, an AI system that discovers over 100 cryptographic misuse vulnerabilities including a critical SSL flaw affecting billions of devices [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Chai, an AI-driven system designed to identify and validate cryptographic misuse vulnerabilities by analyzing naturally occurring signals. Unlike traditional methods that focus on auditing individual codebases, Chai catalogs flaws at the library level and traces them through cryptographic dependency graphs, enhancing detection efficiency. The system has uncovered over 100 vulnerabilities, including a critical flaw in an SSL library used by billions of devices, as well as security issues in libraries supporting a major web browser and prominent Linux distributions. Chai improves upon classical differential testing by leveraging AI to increase precision in detecting genuine security problems and by turning overlooked discrepancies into actionable leads for vulnerabilities in downstream applications. The system was evaluated across widely used cryptographic libraries such as X.509, JWT, and SAML, demonstrating its broad applicability and effectiveness in uncovering significant security risks.

item.title: Researchers introduce DyRef, a two-stage training framework that improves multi-reference image generation performance on the new OmniRef-Bench benchmark with dynamic reward optimization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced DyRef, a two-stage training framework designed to enhance multi-reference image generation (MRIG) performance, particularly in complex scenarios. They also developed OmniRef-Bench, a new benchmark that evaluates models on diverse and numerous reference images, revealing that existing open-source models struggle as complexity increases. DyRef first fine-tunes models with supervised learning and then applies dynamic reward optimization techniques to improve handling of mixed-type references. The framework incorporates Difficulty-aware Advantage Reweighting (DAR) and Discriminative Reward Scaling (DRS) to adjust optimization objectives and amplify reward differences, respectively. Experiments show that DyRef significantly boosts performance on OmniRef-Bench and single-image editing tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness and generalization capabilities in advancing MRIG technology.

item.title: Researchers propose XMSE-aware adaptive Empirical Bayes estimator that interpolates between maximum likelihood and EB shrinkage, improving risk performance under kernel misspecification [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an XMSE-aware adaptive Empirical Bayes (EB) estimator that dynamically balances between maximum likelihood (ML) and EB shrinkage to improve risk performance, particularly when kernel misspecification occurs. This new estimator uses a closed-form oracle mixing weight to ensure it performs at least as well as both ML and traditional EB methods in terms of excess mean squared error (XMSE). The approach is supported by theoretical consistency proofs and oracle regret bounds, and it adapts effectively to different kernel settings.

item.title: Researchers propose In-Context Model Predictive Generation framework combining large language models and physical simulation for open-vocabulary human motion synthesis with improved realism and semantic fidelity [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced the In-Context Model Predictive Generation (ICMPG) framework, which combines large language models (LLMs) with physical simulation to synthesize human motion from textual descriptions. This approach addresses the challenge of balancing semantic accuracy and physical realism by integrating language-based planning with real-time physical feedback, enabling more realistic and semantically faithful motion generation without requiring task-specific retraining. ICMPG operates through two modules: the Context-Aware Motion Generation (CAMG) module, which uses an LLM to interpret and decompose text commands into candidate motion sequences, and the Model Predictive Generation (MPG) module, which evaluates these sequences via physical simulation and semantic alignment to select the best motion. Extensive testing shows that ICMPG generalizes well to diverse and novel commands, outperforming existing methods in producing motions that adhere to both physical constraints and detailed semantic instructions. This framework bridges the gap between semantic interpretation and physical simulation, offering flexibility to incorporate various LLM backbones. Its closed-loop refinement process enhances the versatility and control of text-driven human motion synthesis, promising improvements for immersive digital applications.

item.title: Researchers analyze framing-sensitive behavioral variability in large language models across architectures, highlighting implications for mental health AI interaction consistency and trustworthiness [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have examined how large language models (LLMs), increasingly used in mental health support and sensitive conversational applications, respond inconsistently to semantically similar inputs framed differently. This framing-sensitive variability poses challenges for ensuring stable and trustworthy AI behavior in psychological contexts. The study analyzed multiple instruction-tuned LLM architectures using controlled prompts and found that framing systematically influences model responses, with internal representations reflecting these variations across transformer layers. Layer-wise probing revealed that behavior-related information remains decodable throughout the models, though decoding strength varies by architecture. Experiments also showed that certain representational directions linked to framing can partially steer model behavior. These findings highlight the importance of robustness to contextual framing when assessing the reliability and consistency of conversational AI systems deployed in mental health settings.

item.title: Researchers propose ReaORE, a reasoning-guided progressive framework for Open Relation Extraction using large reasoning models, outperforming baselines on two datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced ReaORE, a reasoning-guided progressive framework designed to improve Open Relation Extraction (OpenRE) by effectively identifying unseen relations between entities in unstructured text. ReaORE addresses limitations of existing methods by employing a two-stage process: relation filtering through multi-aspect reasoning and embedding-based similarity, followed by fine-grained comparative reasoning for precise relation prediction. This approach enables better generalization and distinction of closely related relations compared to previous clustering or direct label generation techniques. Extensive testing on two widely used OpenRE datasets shows that ReaORE outperforms current baseline models, demonstrating its effectiveness in extracting accurate relation labels in real-world applications. The framework leverages large reasoning models to progressively refine relation extraction, enhancing both reliability and discriminative capacity in handling diverse and unseen relation types.

item.title: Researchers identify and compare emotion vectors encoding valence and arousal in two open-source LLMs, revealing differences in layer-wise representation and corpus sensitivity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified and compared emotion vectors that encode valence and arousal in two open-source large language models, Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509 and Gemma-4-E4B-it. Their study reveals that while both models exhibit valence geometry similar to previous findings in Claude Sonnet 4.5, the way valence representations develop across model layers differs significantly between them. Additionally, arousal encoding varies depending on the corpus used for extraction, indicating that emotional cues are unevenly distributed in generated texts. The team extracted emotion contrast vectors across all layers using two model-generated corpora and found that Gemma-4-E4B-it encodes valence strongly in early layers but loses it in later layers, whereas Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509 shows the opposite pattern. Arousal alignment was stronger with stories generated by Gemma than those by Apertus, suggesting corpus sensitivity in arousal representation. The researchers have open-sourced their experiment code and dataset to support reproducible investigation of emotion representations across language model architectures.

item.title: Researchers propose decision-aligned evaluation metrics for uncertainty quantification in machine learning, revealing misalignment in common metrics and introducing prior-weighted utility metrics for improved decision relevance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
