item.description: Researchers have identified that common metrics used to evaluate uncertainty estimates in machine learning, such as negative log-likelihood and expected calibration error, often do not align well with the actual utility of decisions made based on these estimates. They introduce the concept of decision-alignment to assess which evaluation metrics correspond meaningfully to downstream decision-making outcomes. Their analysis reveals that many widely used metrics either misalign with typical decision problems or reflect unrealistic prior assumptions about tasks. To address this, the researchers propose prior-weighted utility metrics, a new class of proper scoring rules designed to provide evaluation that aligns with decision utility. Through benchmark experiments and real-world case studies, these metrics consistently correlate with realized decision benefits, unlike conventional metrics. This work highlights limitations in current uncertainty quantification evaluation practices and offers a principled approach to improve the relevance of such evaluations for practical decision-making.

item.title: Researchers propose EVIS, an event-aware video instructed segmentation assistant using text-guided event queries and object-pixel-hybrid learning to improve referring video segmentation across five benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed EVIS, an Event-Aware Video Instructed Segmentation Assistant designed to improve referring video segmentation by addressing the challenge of videos containing multiple distinct events. EVIS uses text-guided Event Queries to break down complex videos into simpler, event-specific segments, enabling a clearer hierarchical understanding of video content. This approach helps reduce confusion and hallucinations that occur when models treat a video as a single event. The system also incorporates Object-Pixel-Hybrid Learning, which combines fine-grained pixel features with prior object queries to enhance long-term target tracking in videos. Tested across five public benchmarks, EVIS demonstrated strong performance, suggesting its effectiveness in handling the complexities of referring video segmentation tasks.

item.title: Researchers use deep learning and genetic algorithms to design a compact, wideband inverted Doherty power amplifier achieving up to 63% efficiency over 1.9-2.5 GHz with GaN HEMT prototype [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a deep learning-assisted method combining convolutional neural networks and genetic algorithms to design a compact, wideband inverted Doherty power amplifier. This approach integrates load modulation, impedance matching, power combining, and phase compensation into a single pixelated combiner network. A GaN HEMT prototype built using this method achieved peak drain efficiencies between 51% and 63% and maintained 48%-54% efficiency at 6-dB back-off across the 1.9-2.5 GHz frequency range, with output power around 44 dBm. The prototype also demonstrated strong signal quality, achieving an adjacent channel leakage ratio better than -53.2 dBc when digital predistortion was applied. This work showcases the potential of combining deep learning and genetic algorithms for efficient and compact power amplifier design in wireless communication systems.

item.title: Researchers present unsupervised Remote Sensing Foundation Models using ResNet and FPN for onboard disaster change detection without training, enabling efficient anomaly mapping across diverse terrains and sensors [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an unsupervised change detection method for remote sensing that uses a combination of ResNet-based Remote Sensing Foundation Models (RSFMs) and Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN) to identify anomalies in satellite imagery without requiring training. This approach enables satellites to autonomously detect subtle semantic changes between successive orbital passes, facilitating efficient disaster monitoring and anomaly mapping across various terrains and sensor types. The method leverages an untrained FPN architecture, allowing for high-resolution image generation and mapping with minimal computational effort compared to previous trained, patch-based models. By replacing specialized, trained models with these versatile RSFMs, the system eliminates the need for extensive training and development while maintaining high performance and adaptability. This advancement optimizes onboard storage and computational resources, enhancing the capability of Earth observation missions to respond dynamically to detected anomalies and improving the overall efficiency of disaster event monitoring from space.

item.title: Researchers introduce ShareLock, a multi-tool threshold poisoning attack against Model Context Protocol that covertly reconstructs malicious instructions with over 90% success across mainstream LLMs [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ShareLock, a novel multi-tool threshold poisoning attack targeting the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which connects large language models (LLMs) with external tools. ShareLock uses Shamir's threshold scheme to covertly distribute malicious instructions as benign secret shares across multiple tool descriptions, enabling stealthy and fault-tolerant attacks that evade detection. This approach achieves over 90% success in reconstructing harmful prompts across mainstream LLMs, posing significant security risks to systems using MCP. The study evaluated ShareLock through a comprehensive benchmark involving four multi-tool scenarios and experiments on two MCP clients with various LLMs. Results showed that ShareLock outperforms existing single-tool poisoning methods in avoiding detection while maintaining high attack effectiveness. This research highlights emerging vulnerabilities in LLM-driven agent ecosystems and underscores the need for improved security measures against sophisticated multi-tool poisoning threats.

item.title: Researchers find combining absolute, relative, and forecast market features improves deep reinforcement learning policies for energy trading across 40 European markets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that combining absolute, relative, and forecast market features significantly enhances the performance of deep reinforcement learning (RL) policies for energy trading across 40 European markets. Using a fixed Double DQN agent in a pumped-storage arbitrage environment, the study found that integrating these three types of market data leads to more robust and effective trading strategies compared to relying on any single feature family. The study trained policies on Belgian day-ahead prices from 2007 to 2011 and evaluated them on both a later same-market test set and 39 other ENTSO-E market zones. Results showed that using only absolute, relative, or forecast features individually yielded lower performance, while combining absolute and relative features improved results substantially. The best performance was achieved by combining all three feature families, indicating that state representation is a critical component in designing RL policies for energy storage trading, enabling better transferability and decision-making across diverse market conditions.

item.title: Researchers present the Spec Growth Engine, a lightweight framework addressing context explosion and spec-code drift in AI-assisted software development with machine-readable specs and enforced contracts [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced the Spec Growth Engine, a lightweight framework designed to improve AI-assisted software development by addressing two key challenges: context explosion, where AI agents struggle to process entire code repositories effectively, and silent spec-code drift, where code changes without corresponding updates to specifications. The framework uses a machine-readable specification graph with clear contract and design separation, a context assembler that limits AI focus to relevant code ownership paths, a growth protocol prioritizing critical tasks, and a mechanism that blocks merges when specification and code diverge. The Spec Growth Engine integrates established software engineering principles such as information hiding, architectural modeling, and fitness functions into a streamlined, code-coupled system that enforces consistency without the complexity of heavier frameworks like RUP or MDA. This approach aims to maintain alignment between specifications and code, enhancing the reliability and quality of AI-generated software.

item.title: Researchers introduce NuclearQAv2, a 1,240-question benchmark to evaluate large language models' competence in nuclear engineering across boolean, numeric, and verbal tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed NuclearQAv2, a comprehensive benchmark consisting of approximately 1,240 questions designed to evaluate large language models' (LLMs) competence in nuclear engineering. The benchmark covers boolean, numeric, and verbal tasks, aiming to assess not only factual knowledge but also quantitative reasoning and conceptual understanding within this technical domain. NuclearQAv2 was created using a hybrid approach that integrates expert-authored questions, existing datasets, and LLM-assisted generation from specialized technical texts. Testing various LLMs with NuclearQAv2 revealed significant differences in performance across task types. While models generally excelled at factual questions, they faced greater challenges with quantitative reasoning and conceptual tasks. These findings underscore the need for multifaceted evaluation frameworks and position NuclearQAv2 as a scalable tool for assessing LLM capabilities in specialized scientific fields.

item.title: Researchers introduce parametric open-source games as a continuous analogue of program equilibria, establishing equilibrium existence and cooperation thresholds in symmetric 2x2 games [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced parametric open-source games, a continuous extension of program equilibria where players select parameter vectors that are transformed into mixed strategies in finite games. This framework establishes the existence of equilibria and identifies a precise threshold in symmetric 2x2 games where selfish gradient ascent shifts from defection to cooperation. The study also provides a boundary test for parametric program Nash equilibria and extends the model to neural semantics, linking cooperation to the sensitivity ratio between players. The approach demonstrates how internal parameter access can significantly influence learning dynamics and equilibrium outcomes in canonical games. By adjusting the strength of open-source coupling, the model shows that selfish optimization processes can be guided toward cooperative behavior, offering new insights into strategic interactions where agents' decision procedures are interdependent.

item.title: Researchers introduce Mass Index and regularised extended KL divergence to analyze local mass behavior in Bayesian inference beyond global divergences [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced two new mathematical tools, the Mass Index and regularised extended KL (RE-KL) divergence, to analyze local mass behavior in Bayesian inference beyond traditional global measures like KL divergence and ELBO. These tools enable a detailed examination of how Bayesian updating affects local mass distribution, capturing effects not addressed by global objectives. The Mass Index records polynomial and logarithmic decay scales of local mass, while RE-KL provides a set-localized divergence applicable even with singular components. The study demonstrates how power-log likelihood factors and parameter-dependent supports influence local mass, and establishes inequalities for comparing local small-ball masses under different KL directions. Experimental results illustrate these local behaviors, and the associated code has been made publicly available.

item.title: Researchers find fine-tuning LLMs for security classification creates evasion vulnerabilities undetected by standard evaluations, expanding attack surfaces despite improved accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) for security classification can introduce vulnerabilities that standard evaluation methods fail to detect. While fine-tuning improves accuracy on typical test data, it can cause models to rely on brittle token-level indicators that are sensitive to behavior-preserving transformations such as alias substitution and command reconstruction, leading to evasion risks. The study examined Foundation-Sec-8B-Instruct and its base model Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on PowerShell classification tasks, revealing that fine-tuning specializes inherited model structures in ways that expand attack surfaces despite improved baseline performance. The researchers developed a three-tier evasion benchmark that identified specific transformation variants missed by the fine-tuned model but not by the base model. They also proposed a pre-deployment monitoring approach using linear probes and indicator-token tests to detect semantic shifts caused by fine-tuning. These findings highlight that task-specific fine-tuning can inadvertently create brittle classification rules, cautioning against assuming such models are inherently safer. The work underscores the need for comprehensive specification of transformation spaces and ongoing monitoring to ensure robust AI-enabled security systems.

item.title: Researchers propose CIRCLE, a fixed-feature extractor using bidirectional reservoir features and streaming LDA heads for efficient cold-start class-incremental learning without replay or backbone training [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CIRCLE, a novel approach for cold-start exemplar-free class-incremental learning that avoids replay, external pretraining, and backbone training. CIRCLE uses fixed bidirectional two-dimensional reservoir features combined with streaming linear discriminant analysis heads, enabling efficient sample-wise training without task-boundary information or backbone backpropagation. This method addresses the limitations of existing approaches by providing a balance between computational efficiency and performance, especially in scenarios with many incremental tasks. CIRCLE ensembles multiple random reservoir feature sets and averages the outputs of independent classifiers to manage the tradeoff between feature richness and prediction stability. Evaluations on datasets like CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet variants show that CIRCLE performs competitively with fewer tasks and significantly outperforms strong baselines in long-horizon settings, while also training faster than methods relying on backbone updates. Ablation studies confirm the importance of its fixed feature extractor, streaming classifier heads, and ensembling strategy to its success.
